raw.title: Customer Success Lead
raw.description:
💬 Accurx is solving healthcare productivity for the NHS.

For decades, the NHS has struggled with fragmented systems that make simple tasks feel impossible. At Accurx, we’re changing that by building a single, system-wide platform that helps every patient get gold-standard, efficient, and joined-up care.

What started as a way for GPs to text a patient has now evolved into an all-in-one digital toolkit used by 98% of GP practices.

Our platform now powers Total Triage to manage patient demand, and Self-Book, which lets patients schedule their own appointments in seconds. We’ve automated routine care with Patient Questionnaires for long-term conditions, while Accumail finally allows staff-to-staff communication to happen instantly across different care settings. We’re now pushing the boundaries of the consultation itself with Accurx Scribe, our AI-powered note-taker that drafts medical notes in real-time.

We’re not just shipping features. We’re giving clinicians their time back and ensuring every patient journey is as smooth as it should be.

That sounds cool - what does a Customer Success Lead have to do with it?

Accurx works with 41 of the 42 NHS ICBs and is growing fast in secondary care. To keep up with how the NHS is organising itself, our Account Management team has just moved to a regional model, with leads for London, the South and the North. The goal is simple: join up what we’re learning across primary care, secondary care, acute, community and mental health, and make sure the best opportunities get surfaced across the whole of England, not just in one set of ICBs.

We’re hiring a Customer Success Lead for the North. You’ll lead a team of Customer Success Managers across primary and secondary care and be the strategic, zoomed-out view of the region. Your team is close to the accounts. Your job is to spot the patterns across them, turn what they’re hearing into strategy, and help Accurx show up at a regional level.

The challenges you’ll solve as a Customer Success Lead

  • Lead and grow a team of CSMs. You’ll start with three CSMs, each with their own region, customers and stage of the customer journey. You’ll coach them, unblock them and help them do the best work of their careers.

  • Bring two very different care settings together. Primary care is about deepening trust we’ve built over years. Secondary care is about firsts: new services, longer implementations and goalposts that move. You’ll work out what connects them, what doesn’t, and where learnings from one can speed up the other.

  • Turn insight into strategy. Your team will feed you what’s happening on the ground. You’ll spot trends, gaps and duplicated effort across the region and turn them into projects, goals and growth opportunities in products like Accurx Scribe and Total Triage.

  • Own the commercial picture for your region. You’ll keep a close eye on churn, risk, renewals and upsell across your team’s accounts, and represent the region at our weekly business reviews with the exec team.

  • Build the playbook with your fellow leads. The regional model is brand new. Alongside the leads for London and the South, you’ll shape how we work, what best practice looks like and how we scale it.

  • Be the link across the business. You’ll work closely with implementation, transformation, support and business development, making sure the voice of our customers shapes where Accurx goes next.


You should apply if...

  • You’ve led customer-facing teams. You have a few years of people management in customer success or account management, and you love helping others grow.

  • You’ve built things from the ground up. You’ve been on a startup to scale-up journey, worn a lot of hats, and taken customers from never having heard of you to being your biggest advocates.

  • You care about depth, not volume. You’ve looked after long-standing, strategic relationships rather than a high-volume queue, and you know that trust is what makes customers stick.

  • You can zoom out. You don’t need to be in the weeds of every account. You’re great at spotting patterns, asking the right questions and knowing where your team needs you most.

  • You’re comfortable with ambiguity. You’re happy to try something, get it wrong, learn and go again. Process is something you create, not something you wait for.

  • You’re a big collaborator. You’re an incredible communicator and listener, and you know the best outcomes come from working across teams.

  • You’re curious about the NHS. Healthcare experience is welcome but not essential. What matters is empathy for the pressure the NHS is under and the patience to build trust in a complex system.


What’s in it for you?

You’ll join a high-performing team on a mission to solve healthcare productivity, building a platform used by around 300k NHS staff every week, supporting the care of over 50 million NHS patients every year. We set a high bar, move fast, and give people the ownership and support to do the best work of their careers

  • £70,000 - £90,000 salary, plus a discretionary recognition bonus for exceptional performance and impact, nominated by managers and awarded by our leadership team

  • Equity: £30,000 in equal share options, so you share in the value you help create

  • Benefits to suit you: adjust your healthcare cover, your pension or life insurance, whatever stage you’re at in life

  • Built for collaboration: We are an office-first culture and ask that you’re in our (dog-friendly) Shoreditch office for a minimum of 3 days a week

  • Close to our users: Regular hackathons, plus dedicated time to visit GP practices and other healthcare settings to see first-hand how our products are used

  • Time off: You’ll get 28 days of holiday (plus bank holidays) and up to 4 weeks to work from anywhere per year

  • Support at home: We offer enhanced parental leave, fertility support and parental loss support

  • We have our very own chefs: Free healthy breakfasts, snacks and lunches, plus a weekly sweet treat

Compensation: £70K – £90K

raw.title: Account Manager, Enterprise
raw.description:
About Airwallex

Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full.

 

How you'll make impact

You'll manage a portfolio of strategic enterprise customers and grow gross profit through renewals, upsell and expansion across Airwallex's product suite. You'll build trusted relationships with senior commercial, finance, operations, product and technology stakeholders, using strategic account plans, business reviews and customer insight to increase adoption, improve retention and identify new growth opportunities.

  • Grow existing customer accounts through renewals, upsell and expansion across Airwallex's product suite.

  • Build and execute strategic account plans that clarify customer objectives, stakeholder relationships, risks, renewal priorities and future growth opportunities.

  • Lead commercial negotiations, business reviews and cross-sell opportunities that demonstrate value, improve retention and support Net Revenue Retention.

  • Coordinate complex onboarding, escalations and customer initiatives across Sales, Product Sales, Solutions Engineering, Product, Operations, KYC and Onboarding, Legal, Customer Success and other internal teams.

  • Maintain accurate CRM records, opportunity tracking and forecasts while turning customer feedback into product, operational and go-to-market improvements.

You'll work from our London office three days a week.

What we're looking for

Essentials

  • 5 to 6 years of sales or account management experience, including experience managing complex enterprise or strategic customer relationships.

  • A proven track record of retaining and growing existing accounts through renewals, upsell, cross-sell or other expansion motions.

  • Experience managing multi-stakeholder customer relationships, including engagement with senior commercial, finance, operations, product or technology leaders.

  • Strong commercial, communication and negotiation skills, with the ability to simplify complex topics and build trusted relationships internally and externally.

  • Experience working cross-functionally to resolve customer issues, manage escalations and deliver complex onboarding, implementation or post-go-live initiatives.

  • Experience in fintech, payments, financial services, B2B SaaS or another technology environment with complex products. Experience with API-enabled products is an advantage.

Preferred

  • Experience managing enterprise accounts in payments, FX, cross-border payments, treasury, cards, embedded finance or other financial infrastructure products.

  • Experience developing strategic account plans, leading QBRs or executive business reviews, and building relationships with C-level stakeholders.

  • A data-driven approach to account health, forecasting, renewal planning and commercial prioritisation, with strong CRM discipline.

  • Curiosity, resilience and an entrepreneurial mindset, with the ability to operate effectively in a fast-growing environment, adapt to evolving priorities and proactively solve complex customer problems.

You'll thrive here if

  • You have a track record of hitting your numbers, and you’re motivated by stretch goals.

  • You own the outcome and you don't wait for permission to fix what's broken.

  • You connect dots across functions and hold the big picture without losing grip on the details.

  • You simplify complexity rather than hiding behind it.

  • You communicate clearly and directly across cultures, and you're thoughtful about how context shifts meaning across borders.

Learn more about your team

Enterprise Business is about more than closing deals. This team helps large, often multinational organizations solve complex financial challenges that go well beyond a single product decision — moving money globally, managing treasury operations, embedding financial services across borders, and replacing fragmented financial workflows with one global system built to scale. You’ll be helping customers understand what is possible when their financial operations work as one global system.

It's a team for strategic sellers with a builder mindset, who combine strategic thinking with deep product knowledge: comfortable with long deal cycles, multiple stakeholders, and the kind of autonomy that comes from being trusted to create value, shape the deal, and move complex opportunities forward rather than follow a rigid playbook. If you want to work on high-consequence deals that genuinely change how large businesses operate financially, this is the place to do it.

Applicant Safety Policy: Fraud and Third-Party Recruiters

To protect you from recruitment scams, please be aware that Airwallex will not ask for bank details, sensitive ID numbers (i.e. passport), or any form of payment during the application or interview process. All official communication will come from an @airwallex.com email address. Please apply only through careers.airwallex.com or our official LinkedIn page.

Airwallex does not accept unsolicited resumes from search firms/recruiters. Airwallex will not pay any fees to search firms/recruiters if a candidate is submitted by a search firm/recruiter unless an agreement has been entered into with respect to specific open position(s). Search firms/recruiters submitting resumes to Airwallex on an unsolicited basis shall be deemed to accept this condition, regardless of any other provision to the contrary.

Equal opportunity

Airwallex is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and anyone seeking employment at Airwallex is considered based on merit, qualifications, competence and talent. We don’t regard color, religion, race, national origin, sexual orientation, ancestry, citizenship, sex, marital or family status, disability, gender, or any other legally protected status when making our hiring decisions. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

raw.title: Director, Fraud Risk
raw.description:
About Airwallex

Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full.

 

About the Role

As Director, Fraud, you will lead Airwallex’s First Line of Defence (1LoD) Fraud function. You will own the design, execution, and continuous optimization of our global fraud strategy, policies, detection systems, and operational workflows across Airwallex’s financial infrastructure. In this role, you will lead a high-performing team responsible for stopping fraud in real time while keeping friction low for legitimate, high-growth global businesses. Airwallex processes billions in cross-border payments, multi-currency corporate cards, merchant acquiring, and embedded finance products. You and your team will directly defend our ecosystem against card fraud, account takeover (ATO), merchant bust-out, payment scams, and synthetic identities.

You will partner directly with Engineering, Data Science, Product, Legal, and Compliance and interface closely with Second Line Risk to build and operate scalable, AI-native fraud detection models, effective triaging processes and operational guardrails.

What You’ll Do

  • Define & Execute 1LoD Global Fraud Strategy: Direct and build out the operational fraud strategy across all Airwallex products (Global Accounts, FX, Acquiring, Cards, and Embedded Finance / BaaS). Translate enterprise risk appetite set by the board and 2LoD Risk into actionable rules, detection logic, operational policies, and loss-prevention workflows.

  • Lead & Scale the 1LoD Fraud Team: Build, lead, and mentor a world-class team of fraud strategists, analysts, and operations specialists responsible for rule writing, alert triage, incident response, and dispute operations.

  • Optimize Risk vs. Conversion: Own and execute real-time fraud decisioning rules, loss-mitigation frameworks, and chargeback monitoring programs. Drive precision in risk controls to reduce fraud losses without introducing unnecessary friction for legitimate customers.

  • Drive Product & AI/ML Execution: Co-own the fraud product roadmap with Data Science and ML Engineering teams. Directly inform and test next-generation models for real-time transaction monitoring, device fingerprinting, behavioral biometrics, and anomaly detection.

  • Own Partner & Scheme Operational Compliance: Ensure operational adherence to fraud rules, monitoring programs, and threshold limits established by card schemes (Visa, Mastercard, local schemes), banking partners, and regulators across all active markets.

  • Incident Management & Root Cause Remediation: Lead real-time response to complex or high-value fraud incidents. Conduct post-mortems, deploy immediate policy/rule fixes, and implement long-term structural remediations.

  • Metrics & Loss Budget Ownership: Own operational KPIs, fraud loss performance against targets, False Positive Rates (FPR), triage SLAs, and chargeback recovery rates. Serve as the primary operational presenter on 1LoD performance to risk committees and leadership.

Essentials

  • 10+ years of hands-on Fraud Management experience in fintech, payment processing, acquiring, or modern banking infrastructure, with direct experience leading operational 1LoD teams and holding loss budget accountability.

  • People Leadership: Proven track record of scaling, mentoring, and directing high-performing strategy and operational fraud teams in fast-paced environments.

  • Deep Domain Expertise: Comprehensive operational knowledge of merchant acquiring fraud, card issuing fraud, CNP chargebacks, account takeover (ATO), and cross-border payment typologies.

  • Card Scheme Mastery: Deep practical expertise in Visa/Mastercard dispute management, scheme monitoring programs (e.g., VFMP, VAMP, ECM), and payment gateway risk mechanics.

  • Data & Technical Fluency: Hands-on experience working directly with complex data environments and decision engine tooling (SQL, Python/R, real-time risk platforms, rule engines).

  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Demonstrated ability to drive operational execution across Product, Engineering, Data Science, Legal, 2LoD Risk, and external banking partners.

Applicant Safety Policy: Fraud and Third-Party Recruiters

To protect you from recruitment scams, please be aware that Airwallex will not ask for bank details, sensitive ID numbers (i.e. passport), or any form of payment during the application or interview process. All official communication will come from an @airwallex.com email address. Please apply only through careers.airwallex.com or our official LinkedIn page.

Airwallex does not accept unsolicited resumes from search firms/recruiters. Airwallex will not pay any fees to search firms/recruiters if a candidate is submitted by a search firm/recruiter unless an agreement has been entered into with respect to specific open position(s). Search firms/recruiters submitting resumes to Airwallex on an unsolicited basis shall be deemed to accept this condition, regardless of any other provision to the contrary.

Equal opportunity

Airwallex is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and anyone seeking employment at Airwallex is considered based on merit, qualifications, competence and talent. We don’t regard color, religion, race, national origin, sexual orientation, ancestry, citizenship, sex, marital or family status, disability, gender, or any other legally protected status when making our hiring decisions. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

Senior Total Rewards Partner, Total Rewards

How you'll make impact

As Airwallex scales globally and prepares for its next stage of growth, you’ll own and evolve the Total Rewards agenda across compensation, benefits, job architecture, benchmarking, equity governance and pay transparency.

  • Own and evolve global compensation frameworks, salary structures, geographic differentials, market positioning, compensation cycles and financial models that support hiring, retention, executive decision-making and international expansion.

  • Build and improve job architecture and leveling frameworks that support organisational scalability, internal equity and talent mobility.

  • Shape regional and global benefits programmes, including plan design, annual renewals, broker and insurer negotiations, benchmarking and cost optimisation, while balancing employee value, fiscal discipline and local market requirements. Hands-on benefits administration isn’t the primary focus of this role.

  • Partner with executive leadership, People Partners and Talent Acquisition to turn complex reward data into clear recommendations, challenge decisions that conflict with business strategy, market data or regulatory requirements, and lead Total Rewards initiatives from scoping and design through implementation.

  • Support international market expansion by developing competitive, compliant and locally relevant compensation and benefits frameworks across global markets.

What we're looking for

Essentials

  • 7+ years of progressive experience in Total Rewards, Compensation, or Benefits, ideally within high-growth technology or fintech environments.

  • Proven track record of designing, building, and scaling global compensation frameworks, benefits programs, and equity structures in hyper-growth organisations.

  • Strong expertise in compensation strategy, including market benchmarking, job and salary architecture, geographic pay differentials, compensation cycles, and financial modelling.

  • Experience designing benefits programs and leading annual renewals, including broker and insurer negotiations. Hands-on benefits administration is not a primary focus.

  • Practical experience managing compensation planning and equity programs, leading system implementations or migrations, and working with HR technology platforms such as Workday, BambooHR, Carta, Shareworks or Pave.

  • Advanced analytical capabilities, with the ability to translate complex data and financial models into actionable insights and executive recommendations.

  • Proven ability to influence and communicate Total Rewards decisions with senior leaders, People Partners, and Talent Acquisition, demonstrating sound business judgement and confidence in challenging decisions that conflict with business strategy, market data, or regulatory requirements.

  • A builder mindset, with the ability to operate independently, navigate ambiguity, and develop scalable solutions across global markets and time zones.

Preferred

  • Experience in a late-stage private, pre-IPO, or recently listed company, particularly navigating equity program transformation, strengthening rewards governance, and preparing for public-market readiness.

  • Experience building scalable Total Rewards programs from the ground up in a fast-paced, high-growth environment, with end-to-end ownership and strong accountability.

  • Experience advising C-suite and senior leadership stakeholders on compensation, benefits, equity and rewards governance.

  • Strong analytical and financial modelling skills, including scenario modelling and assessment of financial implications.

  • Experience partnering effectively across diverse cultures, functions and international teams, navigating time zones and varying local market requirements.

  • Experience translating complex compensation, benefits and equity concepts into clear, actionable messages for business leaders, People teams and employees.

raw.title: People Operations Manager
raw.description:
About Us

At algo1, we are reinventing one of the world’s most familiar experiences: the in-store grocery trip. We are building an AI-native product that understands each shopper, responds to their context in real time and makes an everyday experience less stressful, more personal and more engaging.


We’re backed by leading investors and founded by two entrepreneurs: one with a track record of building companies, and the other a recognised leader in data and analytics. Together, they have brought together frontier AI researchers and engineers, product and strategy leaders, and senior operators from major UK and US grocery businesses.


The people who join now will have an opportunity to shape the product, the culture, and what algo1 becomes.

The Role
We’re looking for an experienced, hands-on People Operations Manager to help us build and run the people side of algo1 as we grow.

This is a remote, part-time role, working approximately 3-4 hours each day, five days a week. There will be the occasional need to visit our London office to meet key colleagues. You’ll report to our Chief Operating Officer and work closely with our leadership team and hiring managers across the business.

We need someone who is equally comfortable handling the day-to-day essentials of HR administration and providing thoughtful, practical support on broader people matters. One day you might be preparing a contract, organising onboarding or updating employee records. The next, you could be helping a manager prepare for a performance review, working through a people issue or improving one of our HR processes.

You’ll ideally have worked in a startup or small, fast-growing business before, so you’ll understand that there isn’t always a playbook. You’ll know when to follow a process, when to improve one, and when to use your judgement to find a pragmatic solution.

This is a role for someone who enjoys getting things done, takes pride in the details and wants to make a meaningful contribution to a growing business.

What You’ll Own

  • People administration and employee lifecycle. Own the day-to-day people administration, including offer letters, employment contracts, employee records, documentation and changes throughout the employee lifecycle. Ensure everything is accurate, organised and up to date.

  • Hiring, onboarding and off-boarding. Coordinate the operational side of bringing people into and out of the business, ensuring contracts, checks, documentation and handovers are completed smoothly and people have a positive experience.

  • Right to work and immigration. Manage right to work checks and coordinate visa and sponsorship processes where required, maintaining accurate records and ensuring the business meets its obligations.

  • Performance and employee relations. Coordinate performance review processes, support managers with feedback and performance conversations, and help manage employee matters with appropriate documentation, follow-up and escalation.

  • HR guidance and compliance. Act as a first point of contact for everyday people questions, providing practical guidance to managers and employees. Maintain our people policies and processes, ensuring they remain appropriate and compliant as the business grows.

  • People systems and reporting. Own our HR systems and people data, maintaining accurate employee records and ensuring information is accessible, reliable and well organised.

  • Culture and people initiatives. Support employee engagement and wider people initiatives, helping to build a positive, thoughtful and high-performing working environment.

  • Process improvement and operational support. Identify opportunities to simplify, automate and improve how we manage people operations. Work closely with the COO on ad hoc people and operational projects as needed.

About You

Must Have

  • Relevant HR experience. You have a solid background in HR (or ‘People’) Operations, ideally in a generalist or standalone role where you’ve had broad responsibility across the employee lifecycle.

  • Confidence using HR systems, DocuSign and spreadsheets.

  • Strong understanding of UK employment practices. You have a good working knowledge of UK employment law, HR compliance and best practice, and understand when specialist advice is needed.

  • Sound judgement and discretion. You’re comfortable handling sensitive and confidential matters, approaching difficult situations objectively and communicating with empathy and professionalism.

  • A highly organised, detail-oriented approach. You’re methodical, reliable and able to manage multiple priorities without losing sight of the details.

  • An independent, hands-on mindset. You take ownership, use your initiative and are equally comfortable working through tasks independently as collaborating with managers and senior leadership.

  • Clear communication skills. You’re able to build trust across different levels of an organisation and adapt your communication style to the situation.

Nice to Have

  • Startup experience. You’ve worked in an early-stage or small, fast-growing business and understand the realities of building processes while operating in an environment where priorities and structures can change quickly.

  • Experience supporting UK visa and sponsorship processes, including Skilled Worker sponsor licence requirements.

  • A CIPD qualification or equivalent relevant experience.

  • Experience establishing or improving people operations in an early-stage business.

  • An interest in using AI and automation to make people processes more efficient.

How We Work
We’re a fast-moving startup, and we value people who are curious, pragmatic, organised and comfortable taking ownership.

There is flexibility in how those hours are structured, with a working pattern agreed together. You’ll need to be accessible during agreed UK working hours and comfortable collaborating virtually with our team.

We believe great people operations don’t need to be complicated. We want someone who can bring experience and good judgement, keep the essentials running brilliantly and help us build the right processes as we grow.


What We Offer

  • Competitive salary (pro rata).

  • 25 days’ annual leave (pro rata), plus applicable bank holidays.

  • A predominantly remote role.

  • A flexible, part-time working pattern across five days a week.

  • Real ownership and the opportunity to shape our people practices.

  • The chance to work with an ambitious team building an AI-native product from the ground up.

raw.title: Principal Product Designer: UX/UI
raw.description:
About Us

At algo1, we are reinventing one of the world’s most familiar experiences: the in-store grocery trip. We are building an AI-native product that understands each shopper, responds to their context in real time and makes an everyday experience less stressful, more personal and more engaging.

We’re backed by leading investors and founded by two entrepreneurs: one with a track record of building companies, and the other a recognised leader in data and shopper analytics. Together, they have built a team of frontier AI researchers and engineers, product and strategy leaders, and senior operators from major UK and US grocery businesses.

The people who join now will have an opportunity to shape the product, the culture, and what algo1 becomes.

The Role

You'll report to our Head of Design, who sets the overall design direction across our consumer and business applications, brand and website. You'll be our most senior hands-on product designer, owning the UX, UI and design system of our consumer applications, with significant influence over product direction.

We're building something with no established design playbook: a consumer experience that connects the digital and physical worlds of grocery shopping. The challenge is that a store isn't a website. Shoppers are moving, browsing shelves and making decisions in seconds. The store must remain the main event, with our technology playing a supporting role rather than competing for attention.

The hardest part is making this feel intuitive for everyone, from digitally confident shoppers to people who rarely use technology in stores. You'll need exceptional consumer mobile design skills, the curiosity to rethink familiar interaction patterns and the judgement to make sophisticated AI feel effortless.

You'll work closely with product, engineering and machine learning to shape what we build, not just how it looks. You'll have the opportunity to test your ideas with real shoppers, improve existing experiences and invent new ones as we build towards scale. Success will be measured by how much easier and more engaging you make shopping, not by how many screens you design.

This is a senior individual contributor role. You won't manage people initially, but you'll help hire and mentor the designers who join next, set the quality bar and establish how the team works.

How you work matters as much as what you design. We're agentic-first and everyone has access to max-tier AI tools, so you'll never be rate-limited. You'll use AI throughout the design process, from exploration and prototyping to design-to-code and QA, and help us discover better ways to build.

What You'll Own

  • Consumer UX and UI. Own the quality of our mobile consumer experience, from complex journeys and interaction patterns to clear, polished, production-ready screens. Make every interaction feel simple, intuitive and consistent.

  • Connected shopper journeys. Design experiences that move naturally between home and store. Bring digital discovery, planning and personalisation into physical shopping without distracting from the products on the shelves.

  • Product thinking and innovation. Work with product and engineering to define problems, challenge assumptions and shape the roadmap. Invent new interaction patterns where conventional mobile UX doesn't translate to the physical world.

  • The design system. Own the components, tokens, patterns and documentation that keep our consumer experience consistent as we scale. Keep Figma and code aligned, manage contributions and prevent design drift.

About You

Must Have

Your portfolio demonstrates outstanding visual and interaction craft, including excellent hierarchy, layout, typography and attention to detail, alongside strong product thinking and measurable improvements to real user experiences.

Software Engineer, Research Platform

About Us

Basecamp Research is building frontier AI for therapeutic design. We believe the future of medicine lies in reprogramming the body to repair itself, and we design the models and the medicines to teach it how.

Our EDEN models are trained on BaseData and our Trillion Gene Atlas (TGA), the world's largest proprietary genomic dataset, with over 10B genes collected through partnerships in more than 30 countries across all seven continents. This gives our AI models access to genetic diversity that doesn't exist in public databases, and enables EDEN to design cell and gene therapies, enzymes, and peptides directly from information about a disease. Our pipeline of EDEN-designed therapeutics, beginning with in vivo cell therapy, is advancing towards clinical development.

In September 2026 we closed an oversubscribed $140M Series C led by S32, with participation from NVIDIA, Anthropic's Anthology Fund, Catalio, European Tech Collective, Firebrand River Capital, King Philanthropies, NATO Innovation Fund, NVentures (NVIDIA's venture arm), Redalpine, Rockefeller Foundation, Singular, Sovereign AI and True Ventures. We have offices and labs in London and Boston, we partner with biopharma companies and academic institutions worldwide, and our work has been recognised by Fast Company's Top 10 Most Innovative Companies in Biotech, the FT-backed Sifted AI100 list of Europe's leading AI startups as well as Barclays Eagle Labs Ones to watch, AI100.

At Basecamp Research, we pride ourselves on being a lean collaborative and global team with extremely specialist and unique skills. Our biologists, engineers, ML scientists and field explorers are united by a sense of adventure and the belief that AI, biology and data, will result in new medicines for patients who have few options today.

The Role

We're seeking an exceptional Software Engineer, Research Platform to join our team in London, embedded in our AI, genomics and computational biology teams. Your goal is to accelerate their research by bringing production-grade engineering to the systems they depend on.

This is an embedded role. You'll sit with the scientists, understand what they are trying to find out, and build the systems that get them there faster: making research code reliable, reproducible and fast; designing data pipelines and workflows that run at the scale of BaseData and the Trillion Gene Atlas; and building the tools and infrastructure that let a small research team run far more experiments. You'll move between genomics, computational biology and ML work as the research requires, and own what you build end to end.

The engineering problems are substantial: petascale biological data, workflows that span cloud and HPC, and research that is often limited by how quickly an idea can be turned into a result.

You'll report to the Head of Platform as part of our engineering team, which spans London and Boston, and work day to day within the AI research, genomics and computational biology teams in London.

About you

  • A very strong engineering background: complex production systems you have designed, built and owned. Expert in Python; strong habits around testing, code review and CI/CD.

  • You take responsibility for the outcome. If that means learning something new or working outside your usual area, you do it.

  • A solid understanding of data pipelines, workflow orchestration, distributed execution and scalable compute (Kubernetes, HPC, containers).

  • You can take a researcher's code, understand the question behind it, and make it robust without losing what made it useful.

  • A real interest in biology, ideally with experience of genomic, protein or sequencing data. You will learn the science well enough to understand the research, not just its code.

  • Collaborative and low ego. We care about drive, and in a small team everyone depends on what you build.

Nice to have

  • Research or applied experience in computational biology, bioinformatics or genomics.

  • Experience with bioinformatics tooling and sequencing data at scale.

  • Familiarity with Dagster or similar orchestration, Kubernetes, cloud and HPC compute.

  • Experience building tools, MCP servers or workflows that AI agents and researchers use to run computational experiments.

What we offer in return

Impactful Mission: This is a rare chance to do work that genuinely matters. You'll join a talented, fast-moving team, access unique biological datasets at scale, and see your contributions shape real breakthroughs in AI and curative therapeutics.

Collaborative Culture: You'll be surrounded by world-class engineers, scientists, and researchers who care deeply about their work and about each other. With offices in London and Boston, we've built a flexible, cross-functional environment where personal development and real ownership aren't just talking points.

High Growth: We truly believe in investing in our top talent, we make coaching available to team members during steep growth journeys and we have twice yearly promotion opportunities. People who are really successful here own it and go directly to solve problems at pace and we ensure reward increases with impact.

Comprehensive Benefits: We've built a benefits package people value. That means competitive salary, equity, and private healthcare with no medical history exclusions so strong that most employees' family members opt into our plan over their own. We also offer Carrot Fertility with IVF stipend, salary sacrifice pension, bike to work scheme, life insurance, and more.

Do you want to join our team as our new Software Engineer, Research Platform? Then we'd love to hear from you.

We are committed to equal opportunity employment regardless of ethnic or national origin, race, religion, sex, age, citizenship, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, gender identity or any other basis. If you have a disability or additional need that needs accommodating do let us know.

About Boltz

Boltz is a public benefit company building the next generation of AI-powered molecular modeling tools to make biology programmable and accelerate drug discovery, while keeping frontier capabilities broadly accessible.

Boltz began as an MIT spin-out. Our founders built Boltz-1 at MIT, and it became the first fully open-source model to match AlphaFold 3's accuracy in predicting the 3D structure of biomolecular complexes.

We focus on two things:

  • Open foundation models. Boltz-1, Boltz-2, and BoltzGen are open models trusted by 100,000+ scientists across biotech and academia, and used in programs at every Top 20 pharma as well as leading agrichemical and industrial research organizations.

  • Boltz Lab. Our commercial platform runs our latest models and design agents as reliable, production-grade tools built around real chemistry and biology workflows. Teams start from a target and a hypothesis, then generate, evaluate, and rank candidate molecules, while we provide the compute, infrastructure, and collaboration layer so their scientists can move faster.

The two feed each other: open-source adoption earns scientific credibility and community insight, and Boltz Lab turns that into real impact on our partners' discovery programs.

You can read more about our mission, research and product vision in our manifesto.

About the role

As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you will own getting Boltz Lab running inside our enterprise customers' environments, and keeping it running. Large pharma partners often need our platform deployed in their own cloud or tenant, and how fast and smoothly we do that decides how quickly they can start real discovery work; our goal is a full enterprise deployment in under 30 days.

You will work closely with customers' IT, security and cloud teams, our Platform and Product engineers, and our Commercial team.

This role is ideal for someone who likes being the engineer in the room with the customer, is calm when a deployment breaks, and turns every hard install into a faster one next time.

What you'll do

  • Lead deployments of Boltz Lab into customer cloud environments and dedicated tenants, from kickoff to acceptance.

  • Work through each customer's networking, identity, security and compliance requirements, and track blockers to resolution.

  • Support live tenants against agreed service targets: monitoring, upgrades, incident response and root-cause fixes.

  • Automate what you learn into infrastructure-as-code, deployment tooling and runbooks, so each deployment takes less time than the last.

  • Bring what you see in the field back to Platform and Product, from missing features to security and compliance needs (including our SOC 2 and ISO work).

About you

Minimum Requirements

  • Experience deploying and operating production software on cloud infrastructure (e.g. AWS, GCP or Azure), as a DevOps, SRE, infrastructure or solutions engineer. We're hiring at Junior to Senior level.

  • Hands-on with Kubernetes, Docker and infrastructure-as-code (e.g. Terraform), plus solid Linux, networking and scripting (Python or Bash).

  • Working knowledge of enterprise security: identity and SSO, network isolation, secrets management and access control.

  • A track record of getting deployments or migrations over the line under real constraints and deadlines.

  • Clear, confident communication with technical customers, and the judgment to know when to escalate.

Preferred Requirements

  • Experience in a customer-facing engineering role (forward deployed, solutions or implementation engineering), especially with pharma, biotech or other regulated enterprises.

  • Experience running GPU workloads, or ML systems in production; exposure to SOC 2, ISO 27001 or similar compliance work.

  • Early-stage startup experience; experience using Boltz models or open-source contributions.

We know great people don't always tick every box. If this role excites you and you meet most of the minimum requirements, we'd like to hear from you.

What we offer

  • Own how Boltz Lab reaches the world's leading pharma teams.

  • Work alongside one of the most talent-dense teams in the field.

  • Significant ownership and independence, with responsibility for driving projects from concept to deployment.

  • Highly competitive salary with meaningful equity in a public benefit company.

  • Benefits:

    • 25 days plus bank holidays a year

    • Annual team offsite trip

    • Private healthcare (BUPA), covering pre-existing conditions

    • Pension program

    • Paid parental leave

    • Wellhub gym membership

    • Free lunch every day

    • Travel expenses

How we hire

  2. Technical interview: a deployment and troubleshooting scenario

  3. Onsite in London with the team

  4. Offer + Onboarding

Our commitment

Boltz is committed to building a diverse team and an inclusive workplace. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds. If you need any adjustments during the hiring process, tell us and we'll make it work.

raw.title: Senior Data Scientist
raw.description:
Chainalysis is inspired by solving the hardest technical challenges and creating products that build trust in cryptocurrencies. We're a global organization who thrive on the challenging work we do and doing it with other exceptionally talented teammates. Our industry changes constantly, and our job is to create user-facing products supported by our best-in-class data, allowing us to adapt to those rapid changes and bring maximal value to our customers.

We're looking for a Senior Data Scientist to join our Research and Intelligence organisation in London. You'll sit within the Wallet Intelligence Research team focussing on one of the most critical and important data sets in the company and help maintain and build it out through investigative research, behavioral heuristics, graph algorithms, and machine learning techniques. Much of what we work on is state of the art, and often ahead of academia, and your work will directly shape the data that fuels Chainalysis' products and customers across the globe.

This role is ideal for someone who is energised by deeply technical, ambiguous problems at the intersection of data science, graph computation, and on-chain investigation, and who wants to take ownership of projects end-to-end.

In this role, you'll:

  • Own the execution of one or more production data science projects, translating broad problem statements into well-scoped tasks and credible analytical results that meet stakeholder expectations.

  • Design, develop, and validate novel behavioral heuristics and algorithms over blockchain data to attribute on-chain activity and uncover new insights.

  • Apply advanced techniques including graph computation, statistical modeling, and machine learning to large-scale on-chain datasets.

  • Identify and resolve inefficiencies in code, methodology, and workflows; ensure your work integrates cleanly into our production data and tooling stack.

  • Clearly articulate and defend methodology and results to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, maintaining alignment through consistent communication.

  • Mentor junior team members, contribute to technical hiring, and share knowledge.

  • Collaborate closely with peers to bring research from prototype to production.

We're looking for candidates who have:

  • A PhD in computer science, machine learning, statistics, physics, mathematics, or a related technical field – or equivalent industry experience working on advanced, data-intensive problems.

  • Expert-level proficiency in Python and SQL, with a track record of writing clean, testable, production-quality code using agentic workflows.

  • Demonstrated experience applying advanced analytical techniques (e.g. graph algorithms, ML, statistical inference) to large, messy datasets.

  • Comfort working with blockchain data, or strong evidence of the aptitude to ramp up quickly on blockchain data structures and protocols.

  • A demonstrated ability to take ownership of projects: decomposing requirements, driving them to completion, and proactively seeking clarity from stakeholders.

  • An analytical, open-minded approach to problem solving – comfortable navigating ambiguity and willing to dive into problems outside your day-to-day scope.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex methodology to diverse audiences.

Nice to have:

  • Familiarity with Databricks, DBT, Spark/PySpark, or similar large-scale data platforms.

  • Experience modifying infrastructure-as-code (e.g. Terraform) or contributing to production data pipelines.

  • Experience mentoring junior data scientists or engineers.

  • Knowledge of, or passion for, the cryptocurrency and blockchain space.

Technologies we use:

Python

SQL

Databricks

DBT

PySpark / Spark

Terraform

AWS

Postgres

AI at Chainalysis
AI is not a feature at Chainalysis - it is a new way of working. One that turns instructions into work done, and helps us move faster than the threats we're built to counter, and we expect our employees to take ownership of the output and ensure quality. As the world's most trusted blockchain analytics platform, Chainalysis sits at a rare intersection of proprietary data, regulatory relationships and crypto expertise that makes it uniquely placed to shape and lead the next era of AI-driven intelligence - and we expect everyone here, regardless of role, to be an active part of it.

AI fluency is tied directly to how we measure performance and how we plan to win. There is no substitute for your own curiosity. We provide the tools, workflows, and space to experiment - but the expectation is that you develop these capabilities yourself, bring ideas, and collaborate across teams to reinvent the way work gets done. We are not using AI to do less. We are using it to do what was never possible before.

About Chainalysis

Chainalysis is the blockchain data platform, making it easy to connect the movement of digital assets to real-world services. Powered by deep blockchain data and AI, organizations can investigate illicit activity, manage risk exposure, and develop innovative market solutions built on the industry's most trusted blockchain intelligence. Our mission is to build trust in blockchains, blending safety and security with an unwavering commitment to growth and innovation.

You belong here. 

At Chainalysis, we believe that diversity of experience and thought makes us stronger. With both customers and employees around the world, we are committed to ensuring our team reflects the unique communities around us. We’re ensuring we keep learning by committing to continually revisit and reevaluate our diversity culture.

We encourage applicants across any race, ethnicity, gender/gender expression, age, spirituality, ability, experience and more. If you need any accommodations to make our interview process more accessible to you due to a disability, don't hesitate to let us know. You can learn more here. We can’t wait to meet you.

About Codat

Codat is an advisory intelligence solution purpose-built for modern commercial banking. Through rich, specialized data, forward-looking insights, and integrated workflows, Codat empowers banking teams to deepen their relationships, grow their revenue, and simplify their day-to-day work.

Founded in 2017 and backed by JPMorgan, PayPal, Amex, Plaid, and Shopify, Codat has successfully powered over 350,000 connections to business customers’ financial systems — and is trusted by industry leaders to turn scattered information into actionable, strategic advantages in real time, every time.

The Role

We're looking for a Finance Director to lead our finance team at Codat. You'll own the numbers from start to finish: the plan, the monthly close, the board pack and the conversations with our investors.

This is both a hands-on role and a senior role. You'll have one direct report and still do plenty yourself: one day you'll be taking the board through the forecast, and the next you'll be sorting out a payroll query or approving expenses. You'll report to the Chief Legal and Business Officer and work closely with the leadership team on where we spend money and why, and you'll be the person who tells us when the numbers don't support a plan.

What You'll Work On

  • Budgeting, forecasting and cash. You'll build the annual and longer-range plan with budget holders across the business, keep the forecast current and track how we're doing against it. You’ll also own cash flow forecasting and runway, plus headcount planning with the people team.

  • Board and investor reporting. You'll prepare the board pack, covering ARR, unit economics and customer metrics, and the analysis investors and advisers need.

  • The month-end close, management accounts and statutory consolidation across our UK and US entities, including intercompany. You'll also run the annual audit to sign-off and own our technical accounting positions, such as revenue recognition and share-based payments.

  • Group tax and compliance across the UK and US, and our relationships with auditors, tax advisers, lawyers and banks.

  • ARR and revenue modelling. You’ll partner with the team to ensure our commercial reporting keeps pace as the business evolves, covering the impact of product and pricing changes, and the bridge from ARR to recognised revenue. You’ll also work with the commercial team on pricing and contract terms, and what they mean for revenue recognition and billing.

  • Day-to-day finance operations: You’ll work alongside our Senior Finance Manager on AP, AR, billing, payroll and expenses, and share the operational load rather than just overseeing it. , The finance systems stack. We want finance to need less manual work every quarter, and automation and AI tools are part of how we'll get there.

  • A small finance team. You'll set their priorities and help them grow.

You'll Probably Have

  • A professional accounting qualification: ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent.

  • Held a senior finance role at a fast-growing, VC-backed tech or SaaS business, ideally across more than one entity and country. You've sat in board meetings and answered investors' questions yourself.

  • Experience in international tax compliance or managing tax advisers across jurisdictions.

  • A good grasp of SaaS metrics and revenue recognition, and the ability to explain them to people outside finance.

  • Stayed close to the detailed work as you got more senior. You're as comfortable building a model as you are closing the books.

  • The confidence to challenge senior people when the numbers call for it. If the data says a plan won't work, you'll say so.

  • Experience managing a small team and helping them grow.

  • AI is already built into how you work. You’ve used automation and AI to change how a finance function runs, not just to speed up the odd task. You can show us a process or system you’ve rebuilt and what it changed for the team.

How We Work

We're a small team with plenty to do. Things move fast: we'd rather make a sound decision quickly and adjust it than wait for perfect information. What you own is yours from start to finish.

We operate hybrid working but without strict mandates on how many days. We trust you to be around when the team needs you and to deliver what you said you would.

raw.description:
About Codat

Codat is an advisory intelligence solution purpose-built for modern commercial banking. Through rich, specialized data, forward-looking insights, and integrated workflows, Codat empowers banking teams to deepen their relationships, grow their revenue, and simplify their day-to-day work.

Founded in 2017 and backed by JPMorgan, PayPal, Amex, Plaid, and Shopify, Codat has successfully powered over 350,000 connections to business customers’ financial systems — and is trusted by industry leaders to turn scattered information into actionable, strategic advantages in real time, every time.

The Role

Some of the biggest commercial banks in the world already work with us. Their relationship managers would rather spend time with clients than dig through the books to find out what's changed. We're building this for them.

We're building the Advisory Intelligence Platform. It puts Codat's client intelligence inside the assistant a banker already uses, starting with Microsoft Copilot. A banker can ask it anything about a client and get an answer from that client's actual books. If they don't ask, it tells them anyway when something important changes, and suggests what to do.

It's a senior role and a hands-on one. Bankers make real decisions based on what the assistant says, so impressing people in a demo isn't enough. It has to be right. Codat is AI-first, not AI bolted onto SaaS, and we work that way ourselves, with agents handling the repetitive work so engineers can focus on the hard problems. You'll build what you design and look after it once it's live, and you'll have a real say in where we take it.

What You'll Work On

  • The reasoning layer. What goes into the model's context, which tools it calls, and when it should break a question into steps. Every number it gives has to trace back to a source, and it needs to know when to say it doesn't know. That last part is harder than it sounds.

  • Evals. You'll build the eval sets and harness, and do the analysis that tells us whether a change made the assistant better or just different. When a banker corrects an answer, that correction becomes a new test case.

  • Model choice and token economics. Which model should handle which job, and what that costs us per answer. Caching or a smaller model is often enough. For some questions a banker needs the strongest model available, and that's worth paying for.

  • The semantic and signal layers. You'll work on both with the data engineers. That means the definitions the model is allowed to use, and the signals that spot when something changes for a client. How the model uses them is down to you.

  • The agents and MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers behind the assistant. This covers the tools the assistant can call, including the ones that will eventually let it draft that email. You'll work out how they break, and add the tracing we need to see what happened inside an answer.

  • Classical modelling where it beats an LLM. Anomaly detection, peer benchmarks, classifiers. Sometimes the best answer is a simple statistical model, not an LLM.

You'll Probably Have

  • Shipped LLM features that people actually used, and been the person they came to when something broke. You've designed how a model works with tools or structured data, and there are things you'd do differently now.

  • Built evals for your own work, and probably had one mislead you. We'd like to hear what you changed.

  • A feel for numbers, whether that comes from a quantitative degree or from your work. You want the denominator before you believe a percentage, and you notice when a headline figure is really about the mix of the data.

  • Opinions about models that come from using them. You've chosen between models on how well they did and what they cost, and you know when a classical model would do a better job.

  • Good engineering habits in Python or another general-purpose language. That means tested, modular services rather than notebooks. Strong SQL as well, and some experience with CI/CD, Docker, cloud (we're on Azure) and tracing for LLM systems.

  • Led work without having the title. People followed an approach you set because you made the case with evidence, and you can explain the trade-offs to someone who isn't technical.

  • AI as part of how you work, for research and prototyping as well as code.

  • Useful, not essential: fintech, lending or accounting; Spark or Databricks; semantic layers or metric views; fine-tuning.

Don't tick every box? Apply anyway. We're more interested in what you've built and how you knew it worked than in a perfect match.

How We Work

We're a small team with plenty to do. Things move fast: we'd rather ship something useful and improve it than polish it in private. What you build is yours from start to finish.

There's no return-to-office mandate, and you can work hybrid or fully remote. We trust you to be around when the team needs you and to deliver what you said you would. What we don't want is anyone staying online late to prove a point.

Compensation: £98K – £120K • Offers Equity

About Codat

Codat is an advisory intelligence solution purpose-built for modern commercial banking. Through rich, specialized data, forward-looking insights, and integrated workflows, Codat empowers banking teams to deepen their relationships, grow their revenue, and simplify their day-to-day work.

Some of the biggest commercial banks in the world already work with us. Their relationship managers want to spend their time with clients, not digging through the books to find out what's changed. We're building the thing that does the digging for them.

It's called the Advisory Intelligence Platform. It puts Codat's client intelligence inside the assistant a banker already uses, starting with Microsoft Copilot. Ask it anything about a client and it answers from that client's actual books. Don't ask, and it tells you anyway when something important changes.

Every one of those answers sits on data. Someone has to get that data in, shape it, define it and serve it, so the number the assistant quotes is the right one. That's you. You write production software, and you care about the data it moves as much as the code that moves it.

This role is for an engineer who's growing fast and wants room to grow faster. You'll ship from your first weeks, own what you build once it's live, and work alongside data and AI engineers who'll push you. Codat is AI-first, not AI bolted onto SaaS, and we work that way ourselves: agents take the repetitive work, engineers take the interesting problems.

What You'll Work On

  • The data behind every answer. Services and pipelines that take raw data from accounting platforms, banks and payment systems and turn it into something a model can trust. When a source sends rubbish, your code notices.

  • The semantic layer. The definitions the model is allowed to use: what counts as revenue, when a month ends, which currency. Get it right and every answer agrees with every other answer.

  • The signal layer. Spotting when something changes for a client: a customer paying later, cash running tighter, a supplier quietly becoming critical. You'll help build the detection and make it fast and reliable.

  • The tools the assistant calls. MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers and APIs that serve data to agents. You'll build them, test them and find out how they break before a banker does.

  • Keeping the numbers honest. Tests, data checks and observability that prove a number is right, and catch it the moment it isn't.

You'll Probably Have

  • Shipped production software that real people depended on, and written most of it yourself. Services, APIs or data systems with tests, not notebooks or config.

  • Had data be the hard part. A source that sent duplicates, a schema that changed under you, two teams who meant different things by "customer". You fixed it, and you'd design it differently now.

  • Good engineering habits in Python, C# or another general-purpose language. Tested, modular code the next person can change without fear.

  • An eye for SQL. You can read a query and tell whether it's right, whoever or whatever wrote it.

  • Stayed on the hook for something after it went live. You found out why it broke, fixed the cause, and added what would have caught it sooner.

  • Some time with CI/CD, Docker and cloud (we're on Azure). You've changed a pipeline, not just pushed to one.

  • A habit of asking why. If someone asks for a number the data can't support, you say so.

  • AI as part of how you work, and you can explain and defend what it helped you build.

  • Momentum. More ownership with each move, new stacks picked up quickly, things built that nobody asked for.

  • Useful, not essential: fintech, lending or accounting; Spark, Databricks or dbt; anything that puts data in front of an LLM.

Don't tick every box? Apply anyway. We're more interested in what you've built and how fast you're growing than in a perfect match.

How We Work

We're a small team with plenty to do. Things move fast: we'd rather ship something useful and improve it than polish it in private. What you build is yours from start to finish.

There's no return-to-office mandate, and you can work hybrid or fully remote. We trust you to be around when the team needs you and to deliver what you said you would. What we don't want is anyone staying online late to prove a point.

Content Lead
raw.description:
Content Lead

Reporting to: CMO

Location: London (hybrid, 4 days a week in the office)

Salary: £80,000-£100,000 + equity

About Electric Twin

Most organisations make their biggest decisions on a thin slice of evidence - a handful of customer calls, one survey, instinct when the data runs out. Electric Twin changes that. We build synthetic audiences: simulations of real groups of people, grounded in research data. Teams ask them questions, test ideas and explore how people might respond, and get answers in minutes that would otherwise take weeks.

The work is grounded, and the science is real. We've run over 40,000 evaluations across populations covering 155 countries. Independent academic research with Professor Michael Muthukrishna at the LSE found our outputs come back roughly 10,000x faster than traditional methods, at 95% accuracy. Customers including The Times, Sage, Virgin, Vodafone and Wingstop use Electric Twin to bring customer insight into decisions about campaigns, products, pricing and strategy.

Electric Twin was founded by Dr Ben Warner (former Chief Data Advisor to the UK Prime Minister) and our CEO, Alex Cooper (a former senior military commander and Director of Mass Covid Testing in the pandemic). We're backed by Atomico, LocalGlobe, Mercuri and angels including Marc Andreessen. We're a team of engineers, AI researchers, behavioural scientists and operators - careful with the science, careful with the responsibility.

The role

We're hiring our first Content Lead to own content at Electric Twin, from the strategy through to what goes out each week.

Our ambition is to make understanding people a normal part of making decisions. Content is central to that: helping people understand a new category, showing what's possible and giving them evidence they can trust.

There's a lot to work with: research, founder perspectives, customer evidence, existing content, and scientists and customers with interesting stories to tell. What's missing is one person who sets the direction and runs the operation day to day.

You'll work closely with our CMO and our product marketer. Our Head of Growth runs the engine - the channels and programmes that reach and convert our audience. Product marketing and content provide the fuel. Product marketing owns positioning and messaging. You’ll take it, turn it into compelling stories and get them out across every channel.

This is a hands-on role. You'll set the strategy and direct agencies and freelancers, and you'll also spend a meaningful part of your week writing and editing.

What you'll do

Strategy

  • Own our content strategy. Take our positioning, messaging pillars and core messages, and decide what we turn them into, where each piece goes and how it lines up with our SEO, AI and PR work.

  • Shape the category narrative. Synthetic audiences are new to most of our buyers. Help them understand the category, see what's possible and find evidence they can trust.

  • Plan content across the buying journey. Earn attention at the top of the funnel, then build out the mid-funnel, where we have the biggest gap today, with content that helps people evaluate us. Know what each piece is for and what it should help someone do next.

Writing and publishing

  • Write and edit. Founder LinkedIn posts, articles, website copy, reports, campaign content and nurture emails. Make complex ideas clear and relevant to the people we want to reach.

  • Develop our founders' voices. Work with our founders, Ben and Alex, to turn their experience and perspectives into distinctive content, particularly on LinkedIn.

  • Repurpose and distribute. Take research, customer stories, product launches and product marketing insight, and adapt them for each channel. Work with growth to get them in front of the right people.

  • Run the editorial plan. Own the publishing calendar across LinkedIn, the blog and email, so everyone knows what’s going out and when.

Building the function

  • Build the content operation. Briefs, editorial standards, production workflows, approvals and a reliable publishing rhythm. Use AI to build repeatable systems for researching, creating, adapting and distributing content, while keeping it accurate, original and high quality.

  • Direct external support. Brief and manage our agency partners and freelancers, set clear priorities and hold their work to a high standard.

  • Partner with performance. Work closely with growth, bringing a good understanding of how content drives growth. Track how it contributes to reach, engagement, organic discovery and pipeline, and use that to decide what we make next.

Your first six months

  • Set our content strategy - building on our positioning, messaging pillars and the content we already have.

  • Take full ownership of the editorial plan, with a consistent publishing rhythm across LinkedIn, the blog and email.

  • Fill the mid-funnel, so buyers evaluating Electric Twin have the content they need to move forward.

  • Make Ben and Alex distinctive voices on LinkedIn, with a regular cadence of posts that sound like them.

  • Launch nurture email beyond product comms.

  • Get the content operation running, with clear briefs, editorial standards, AI workflows, and agency partners and freelancers producing work to a high standard.

What we're looking for

Experience

  • You've owned content strategy and delivery at a B2B technology company, and can show how your work helped build its reputation and commercial growth.

  • You've built or substantially improved a content operation in a fast-moving company where processes and priorities were still taking shape.

  • You've worked with founders or senior leaders, capturing their thinking and developing a voice that sounds like them.

  • You've owned channels end to end, from the idea through to publishing, learning and iterating. You've created content for awareness, consideration and evaluation, and you understand SEO, search intent and what works natively on each channel.

  • You've partnered with product marketing and growth, and briefed and managed agencies and freelancers. You have a network of freelancers and agencies you can call on to scale our content.

Skills and approach

  • An excellent writer and editor. You find the interesting angle, interview experts well and turn complicated subjects into clear, engaging content.

  • Comfortable with strategy and execution. You can produce a high-level plan on your own, then write the first piece yourself.

  • You've used AI to build repeatable content workflows, and you can judge when the output is good enough and when it isn't.

  • Careful with the details. You're comfortable getting to grips with AI, research and technical subjects, you ask good questions and you check claims carefully.

  • You take ownership and think ahead. You spot what needs doing, make a recommendation and see it through, and you give people time to contribute.

  • You're happy taking feedback and you make getting things done easy.

  • Experience producing video content for social channels including YouTube and TikTok.

What we offer

  • £80,000-£90,000 base

  • Meaningful equity in a high-potential seed-stage company

  • Unlimited leave. Take the time you need

  • Generous matched pension contributions

  • Private healthcare

  • Cycle to work scheme

  • Founding content hire with real influence over how the function is built

  • Direct access to and collaboration with world-class founders

  • Hybrid working from our London office (4 days in office a week)

  • Flexible working around life commitments. We value outcomes over presenteeism

When you apply, please share examples of your writing and a content strategy or operation you've built, explaining your contribution and what it achieved.

raw.description:
Reporting to: CMO
Location: London
Salary: £50,000 - £60,000

At Electric Twin, we help organisations understand how their customers might respond before they make a decision. Our synthetic audiences let teams ask questions, test ideas and explore different possibilities in minutes.

Events are an important part of how people discover us, experience our product and build relationships with our team. From international conferences and exhibitions to private dinners, roundtables and partner events, we want every event to have a clear purpose and be delivered brilliantly.

We’re looking for an Events Manager to take ownership of our events strategy and delivery. You’ll help decide where we show up, what we do there and how we turn each event into valuable relationships, compelling content and commercial opportunities.

Why join us now

Electric Twin was founded in 2023 by Dr Ben Warner, former Chief Adviser on Digital and Data to the UK Prime Minister, and our CEO Alex Cooper, a former senior military commander who led the UK’s mass testing effort during COVID.

Today, we’re a team of more than 35 people based in London, bringing together engineers, AI researchers, behavioural scientists and commercial teams. Our customers include The Times, Sage, Virgin and Wingstop, and we’re backed by investors including Atomico, LocalGlobe and Mercuri.

Our ambition is to make understanding people a normal part of making decisions, helping organisations consider how their choices will affect the people who matter.

Events have emerged as one of our most important growth channels this year, and they’ll play an even bigger role in 2027. You’ll build on what we’ve learned to shape a calendar and an approach that we can scale: choosing the right opportunities, delivering memorable experiences and making sure every event has thoughtful follow-up and measurable results. And very importantly, building a delivery system that can scale.

You’ll report to the CMO and work closely with Operations, Partnerships, Sales and the wider marketing team. This is a hands-on role, with space to try new ideas and shape the approach as we grow.

What you’ll do

  • Shape our events strategy. Build and manage an events calendar that supports our marketing and commercial priorities. Recommend which conferences to attend, sponsor or speak at, and where we should create our own events.

  • Own delivery from start to finish. Manage venues, organisers, suppliers, stands, production, registration and on-site delivery. Work closely with Operations on travel, accommodation, shipping and other logistics, keeping responsibilities and deadlines clear.

  • Make every event feel like Electric Twin. Own the brief for what we produce and how it looks, from stands and signage to presentations, demos and supporting materials. Work with design, content and product marketing to deliver a consistent, high-quality experience.

  • Build the content around each event. Coordinate invitations, promotion, speaker preparation, photography, video and post-event content so the value extends beyond the people in the room.

  • Get the right people there. Partner with Growth, Sales and Partnerships on target audiences, guest lists, outreach and pre-booked meetings. Develop joint events that help us reach relevant audiences through our partnerships channel.

  • Drive event follow-up. Agree the follow-up plan before each event, then ensure contacts and conversation notes are captured in HubSpot, assigned to the right people and followed up promptly. Track progress with Sales through to meetings and opportunities.

  • Own the events budget. Forecast the full cost of each event, negotiate with organisers and suppliers, track commitments and actual spend, and recommend where to invest.

  • Report on results and improve the approach. Set objectives and measures for each event. Give the CMO clear updates on delivery, budget, risks and results, including audience quality, meetings, qualified opportunities and pipeline contribution. Run debriefs and apply what you learn.

How we work

We’re building something ambitious, and we like working with people who have ideas and get stuck in. You’ll find scientists, engineers and commercial people who are curious about the world, serious about their work and also happy to question how we do things.

We operate as a team, we help each other out and make sure we keep our eyes on the prize.. You’ll have room to make decisions and try things. We will learn together and keep improving. We also have an expectation that you’ll follow through and keep people in the loop. We care about doing good work - and we enjoy working together.

Your background looks something like

  • You’ve managed B2B events from planning through to delivery and follow-up, ideally within a technology or growing business.

  • You have experience across conferences, exhibitions and smaller hosted events such as executive dinners or roundtables.

  • You’ve helped shape an events calendar and can explain why an event deserves the time and budget.

  • You’re confident managing budgets, negotiating with suppliers and keeping several projects moving at once.

  • You know how to brief creative and content teams, and have a good eye for how a brand should appear in person.

  • You’ve worked closely with Sales and marketing teams on invitations, lead capture, follow-up and reporting.

  • You’re comfortable using a CRM such as HubSpot and turning event data into useful recommendations.

  • Experience delivering international events, particularly in the UK and US, would be valuable.

  • You know how to turn one offs into systems with AI.

As a person, you…

  • Are organised! You take ownership and everyone is informed and on track.

  • Are able to anticipate, spot what needs improving and are keen to make it better
    Care about the details, from the quality of a presentation to whether every guest receives the right follow-up.

  • Have sound commercial judgement and ask what each event should achieve.

  • Build good relationships with colleagues, partners, speakers and suppliers.

  • Stay calm when plans change and are happy to get stuck in on the day.

  • Enjoy combining creative ideas with disciplined planning and delivery.

If you’re curious, we we’d love to hear your experience.
