raw.title: Junior Software Developer
raw.description:
The Software Developer I, Connector role supports Trial Interactive’s proprietary platform, Connector - the cloud-based integrations that move life science data between clients’ clinical systems (for example EDC/eCRF and IRT systems) and Trial Interactive’s life science products. Working under the guidance of senior engineers, the role helps build and maintain connectors, keeps client data flowing accurately, and resolves issues when it does not.

This is a blended role, covering development and maintenance up until handling client requests. This role works closely with the Solutions, DevOps and Engineering teams.

DESCRIPTION

As part of the Development and maintenance responsibility, the resource handles:

• Develop, test and maintain connector components in C# on .NET (AWS Lambda), including the parsers and mappers that convert source-system data (API payloads, files) into the formats required by the Trial Interactive CTMS and eTMF.

• Configure and extend mappings for new studies, sites and visit/status definitions on existing connectors, reusing existing modules wherever possible.

• Assist in the technical onboarding of new clients and studies: connector configuration, test runs in non-production environments, and verification before go-live.

• Work with the AWS services connectors are built on (Lambda, SQS, S3, EventBridge/Step Functions, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch) and make small, reviewed infrastructure changes using Terraform under supervision.

• Consume, test and troubleshoot REST APIs (client/vendor APIs and Trial Interactive import APIs) using code and tools such as Postman, and help extend APIs that improve connector stability and connectivity.

• Write unit and functional tests; use Git (feature branches, merge requests, environment branches) and follow the team’s code review and release process.

• Keep code, configuration and change records documented so that others can maintain them.

• Work on special projects, such as local test environments using LocalStack.

As part of handling Client communication, support and ticket resolution, the resource does:

• Own assigned support tickets from triage to closure: reproduce the issue, investigate, fix or escalate, and record the outcome in the ticketing system (for example Jira, ServiceDesk Plus).

• Investigate data issues end to end – trace a record from the source payload through the archive, parser, connector database and logs to its CTMS/eTMF import result – and establish the root cause (RCA) with evidence.

• Reconcile source-system data against the CTMS/eTMF when a client reports missing or mismatched subjects, visits or statuses, and explain any differences.

• Communicate with clients and Solutions Engineers by email, tickets and calls: acknowledge requests promptly, ask clear clarifying questions, give regular status updates, and explain findings and next steps in plain language.

• Monitor connector health (CloudWatch logs, failed imports, notifications) and respond to failures within agreed response times.

• Escalate appropriately to senior engineers, DevOps or the vendor, with a concise summary of what happened, when, in which environment and for which records.

• Write up RCAs, fixes and known issues so that repeat problems are resolved faster, and help keep support documentation current.

• Handle client and clinical data with care: use the minimum data needed, never share one client’s information with another, and follow Trial Interactive data-protection and change-control procedures.

General

• Keep learning the connector platform, the clinical-trial data domain and cloud and software development best practices.

• Complete all other tasks that are deemed appropriate for this role and assigned by the manager/supervisor.


REQUIRED SKILLS

• Clear written and spoken English, with the ability to explain technical issues in plain language to non-technical clients and to write concise ticket updates and emails.

• A client-service mindset: responsive, calm under pressure, and takes ownership of a ticket until it is resolved or properly handed over.

• Strong problem-solving and debugging skills: forms a hypothesis, checks logs and data, and proves the root cause with evidence before concluding.

• Strong attention to detail with data, such as identifiers, dates, time zones and character encodings.

• Good time management: balances planned development work with interrupt-driven support, prioritizing by client impact.

• Works collaboratively within a team, asks for help early, and is self-motivated and eager to learn.

REQUIRED EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor’s degree or its equivalent in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field.

• 0–1 years of experience in software development, technical support or cloud-based application support; internships and substantial academic or personal projects count.

• Working knowledge of C# and the .NET framework: able to read and debug existing code and deliver small features.

• Familiarity with AWS, particularly Lambda, S3, SQS and CloudWatch Logs.

• Working SQL skills (joins, filtering, aggregation) on relational databases, preferably MySQL.

• Understanding of REST APIs and of JSON, XML and CSV data; experience calling APIs with Postman or similar tools.

• Understanding of data parsing and mapping techniques, including handling of dates, null values and encodings.

• Experience or familiarity with version control systems (e.g., Git).

DESIRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

• Experience with LocalStack for local AWS cloud application development.

• Familiarity with Terraform or other infrastructure-as-code tools.

• Knowledge of CI/CD pipelines and deployment automation.

• Prior experience in customer-facing support, or with ticketing tools such as Jira or ServiceDesk Plus.

• Exposure to clinical research systems and concepts (EDC, CTMS, eTMF; study, site, subject, visit) or to regulated (GxP) software environments.

• Scripting (Python or shell) for data checks and log analysis.

• Familiarity with containerization and microservices architecture.

raw.title: Chief of Staff - UK (f/m/d)
raw.description:
At Upvest, we are on a mission to make investing as easy as spending money. Upvest empowers businesses to offer a wide range of investment products and the best experience in the field of capital market investment and retirement planning. Upvest’s Investment API is easy to integrate so that fintechs and financial institutions can save resources and fully focus on their core business.

Upvest is one of the few fintechs in Europe that can provide its B2B clients with the full range of investment opportunities in the areas of principal broking business, proprietary trading, and safe custody business for traditional securities. We are proud to partner with some of Europe’s largest financial institutions such as Revolut, N26, Raisin, Openbank, Zopa and DKB. Upvest brings together over 300 talented professionals and is backed by leading investors such as Sapphire Venture, Bessemer Venture Partners, BlackRock and Earlybird.

In early 2025 we became FCA-authorised and launched in the UK, and we are already live with some of the UK’s leading financial institutions, such as Zopa, Webull UK and Plum.

We are scaling fast and investing heavily in our UK team and client base. We’re now looking for a Head of Strategy UK to work directly with our General Manager UK, Symmie Swil, and help us continue to grow Upvest’s presence in the UK market.

This role will give you the opportunity to:

  • Shape Upvest’s UK business and strategy to establish the leading investment infrastructure for fintechs, banks, brokers and wealth managers

  • Play a critical role in scaling a growing business, acting as an extension of the general manager and collaborating with senior leadership to execute strategic goals, enable revenue growth and support our clients to scale

  • Work with our UK clients and cross-functionally with growth, product, operations, legal, compliance and strategy teams to deliver impactful change

  • Lead high-impact, cross-functional programmes, gaining broad exposure across the business and industry

  • Build external relationships with clients, ecosystem partners and industry/policy bodies to provide external insights and inform best practice

  • Help us build and maintain a dynamic and collaborative culture in the UK team as the foundations for a successfully scaling business

What you’ll do:

  • Develop and drive the UK Strategy: Help define and deliver the overarching strategy and support the management of the business - from leading key projects to supporting with board reporting, OKRs and budgets.

  • Lead major cross-functional strategic initiatives and projects: Work with teams across the business to drive high-impact initiatives from new product and client launches to GTM planning and regulatory change projects

  • Go-to-market and client engagement: Work alongside the GM and commercial teams on UK go-to-market planning, pipeline and business development, and on strengthening client relationships. Represent Upvest with ecosystem partners and industry and policy bodies, and bring back insight that sharpens our strategy.

  • Corporate governance: Support and maintain robust governance practices within the UK regulated entity - working closely with our legal, compliance and operations teams (e.g. audits, committees, controls and reporting etc.)

  • Drive continuous improvement and operational excellence - lead process improvements, facilitate cross-team communication, drive team effectiveness and cultural initiatives (e.g. team events and offsites)

What you bring:

  • You have 5+ years in wealth / retail investment, banking, fintech or consulting, with strategy and commercial exposure and a solid understanding of how regulation shapes a regulated financial business. Knowledge of the wealth / retail investment industry, its trends and its competitive landscape is highly desirable.

  • You have hands-on GTM or business development experience: you’ve helped win, launch or grow B2B clients or partners, and you can turn client needs into outcomes. Experience in financial services sales or enterprise account management is ideal.

  • You have a strong track record of leading complex, cross-functional programmes end-to-end, from scoping and sequencing to delivery across multiple stakeholders. You are comfortable in taking decisions and show true ownership

  • You are analytical & show business acumen: You are structured and numbers-driven, comfortable building business cases, market sizing and competitive analysis, and working with budgets and repeatable launch playbooks

  • You have demonstrated strong leadership and communication skills, effectively engaging internal and external stakeholders to drive change

  • You thrive in ambiguity and enthusiastically take the initiative to drive improvements; you have multiple examples of taking responsibility and creating roles and opportunities for yourself

  • You enjoy building relationships with clients/partners and have experience working with them collaboratively to solve problems and achieve shared goals

  • You are AI-native - you use AI tools proactively in your day-to-day work (synthesis, reporting, research) and are always looking for smarter, faster ways of working

  • You enjoy being the glue in the team and shaping the culture within it.

We are committed to being a flexible employer, as we understand you don't have to be in the office to do your best work, however this role is based in London (Shoreditch) and ideally you will be able to join us in the office 3 days per week.

How we Upvest in you:

  • Best-in-class AI tools: Every Upvenger has €20,000 per year to spend on the best AI tools available — so you're always working with the most powerful models and tooling on the market.

  • Impact-driven work: We’re building the infrastructure that will power the future of investing in Europe. It’s complex, ambitious, and meaningful. You’ll work with modern technologies and create something entirely new. No legacy systems, no limits.

  • Wellbeing: Recharge with 30 days of annual leave and maintain a healthy lifestyle with sports benefits. Access confidential professional coaching and enjoy the flexibility to work remotely abroad for up to 183 days a year. Recharge with UpRest, a one-month fully paid sabbatical after every 4 years of working at Upvest.

  • Development: Growth is in our DNA. Each Upvenger has access to a personal development budget and the freedom to decide how to use it.

  • Flexible work environment: Work from any of our hubs in Berlin, London or Tallinn hybrid or remotely across Europe, depending on the role. We give you the choice and budget to work where you’re most comfortable and productive, either at home or in the office. You choose.

  • Compensation and equity: We believe that all Upvengers contribute to our success and deserve a competitive, above-market salary and a participation in our employee equity program.

  • Team celebrations: Participate in company-wide events, such as UpFest, dinners, offsites and our Holiday party, to connect with colleagues and celebrate our achievements.

  • Inclusion: We’re committed to a culture where everyone belongs and thrives. Our Employee Resources Groups foster inclusion and connection, like Upfem for our female Upvengers, or UpVergent supporting neurodivergent Upvengers and allies.

Our Values:

  • Make it easy for others. We simplify the complex and act with the best intentions.

  • Own the outcome. We are proactive, fast and confident to get the job done, valuing progress over perfection.

  • Rise to the challenge. We aim high and push the boundaries. We stay curious, learn and celebrate our wins together.

  • Tell the story. We start with the Why to align on purpose. We are transparent and share knowledge to empower and inspire others.

Upvest is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

raw.description:
Applied Intuition, Inc. is powering the future of physical AI. Founded in 2017 and now valued at $15 billion, the Silicon Valley company is creating the digital infrastructure needed to bring intelligence to every moving machine on the planet. Applied Intuition services the automotive, defense, trucking, construction, mining and agriculture industries in three core areas: tools and infrastructure, operating systems, and autonomy. Eighteen of the top 20 global automakers, as well as the United States military and its allies, trust the company’s solutions to deliver physical intelligence. Applied Intuition is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, with offices in Washington, D.C.; San Diego; Ft. Walton Beach, Florida; Ann Arbor, Michigan; London; Stuttgart; Munich; Stockholm; Bangalore; Seoul; and Tokyo. Learn more at applied.co.

We are an in-office company, and our expectation is that full-time employees primarily work from their Applied Intuition office 5 days a week. However, we also recognize the importance of flexibility and trust our employees to manage their schedules responsibly. This may include occasional remote work, starting the day with morning meetings from home before heading to the office, or leaving earlier when needed to accommodate family commitments. This in-office expectation does not apply to contractor positions

About the role

We are looking for an experienced attorney to join our legal team and support our growing business across Europe, and the Middle East. This is a strategic role in a region that is increasingly important to Applied Intuition. You will cover a broad mix of work: sales and procurement contract support, regulatory counseling, and employment matters across our operations in Germany, Sweden, the UK, and the Middle East. In short, this role will make a lasting business impact. You will work closely with Engineering, Policy, People, Sales, and Procurement teams, and you will help shape how Applied works with local regulators as autonomy and AI rules take shape across the region.

Our ideal candidate is a business-minded generalist who is focused on execution, comfortable moving between a vendor agreement, a regulatory question, and an employment issue in the same day, and able to make thoughtful, creative decisions. The role needs a high degree of self-sufficiency, and also someone who enjoys being part of a supportive team dedicated to giving our internal clients excellent legal service. You must be willing to roll up your sleeves and be comfortable working in ambiguity.

 

At Applied Intuition, you will:

  • Draft, structure, and negotiate a range of commercial agreements, including customer sales agreements, procurement and vendor contracts, NDAs, and partnership agreements with automotive OEMs, suppliers, AV companies, and others in the mobility ecosystem.

  • Advise on the regulatory frameworks that govern our products in EMEA, including vehicle type-approval and safety regimes (e.g., UNECE WP.29, EU type-approval), autonomous driving rules (e.g., the German Autonomous Driving Act, the UK Automated Vehicles Act 2024), and the EU AI Act and other emerging AI rules.

  • Counsel the Policy team on engaging with automotive and transport regulators across the region (e.g., the KBA in Germany, and the Swedish Transport Agency), and help shape Applied’s regulatory strategy for autonomy and AI products.

  • Counsel the business on data protection and privacy compliance under the GDPR, UK GDPR, and Saudi Arabia’s PDPL, including vehicle and sensor data, cross-border transfers, and data processing agreements.

  • Advise on employment matters across EMEA, including hiring, employment contracts, policies, works council and co-determination matters, and terminations in Germany, Sweden, the UK, and Saudi Arabia, working with outside counsel as needed.

  • Be a trusted advisor to regional and global leadership on legal matters critical to the growth of the business.

  • Proactively take on other work that comes up as part of a small legal team in a high-growth company.

We're looking for someone who has:

  • Qualification to practice law in Germany (Volljurist/Rechtsanwalt) or England & Wales (Solicitor/Barrister), or an equivalent EMEA legal qualification

  • 6+ years of relevant experience at a top law firm and/or in-house

  • Substantive regulatory experience in one or more of: automotive/vehicle regulation, autonomous driving, data protection, or AI regulation

  • Experience drafting and negotiating commercial agreements, including sales, procurement, and technology agreements

  • Working knowledge of employment law in at least one EMEA jurisdiction

  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment with exceptional organizational skills, juggling competing priorities across multiple practice areas and jurisdictions

  • Fluent English; professional German is a strong plus

Nice to have:

  • Experience with the legal and regulatory environment in Sweden and/or Saudi Arabia

  • Direct experience with vehicle type-approval, UNECE regulations, or automated driving system approvals

  • Experience implementing EU AI Act compliance programs

  • Experience supporting cross-border matters involving U.S. and EMEA stakeholders, or working in the European office of a U.S. company

  • A mix of law firm and in-house experience

  • A computer science, engineering, or other technical background

  • Prior experience in technology, automotive, mobility, or other deep-tech industries

Compensation at Applied Intuition for eligible roles includes base salary, equity, and benefits. Base salary is a single component of the total compensation package, which may also include equity in the form of options and/or restricted stock units, comprehensive health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance coverage, 401k retirement benefits with employer match, learning and wellness stipends, and paid time off. Note that benefits are subject to change and may vary based on jurisdiction of employment.

Applied Intuition pay ranges reflect the minimum and maximum intended target base salary for new hire salaries for the position. The actual base salary offered to a successful candidate will additionally be influenced by a variety of factors including experience, credentials & certifications, educational attainment, skill level requirements, interview performance, and the level and scope of the position.

raw.description:
At Axle Energy, we’re building the infrastructure that will underpin the decarbonised energy system. Our software moves energy usage to times when electricity is cheap and green, by controlling vehicle charging, heating systems, and home batteries. We control hundreds of thousands of energy assets.

We’re building in a legacy industry and moving gigawatt-hours of electrons in the real world, but we operate at lightning speed, and we’re growing the team to meet customer demand.

We’re proud to be supported by world-leading investors, including Energize Capital and Accel.

Read more about what we’re building here.

This role is for someone who can drive go-to-market success and build a repeatable commercial motion as Axle grows.

You’ll help customers adopt our technology, commercialise flexibility across their customer base, and expand usage over time. You’ll be expected to move quickly, remove friction, and adapt processes pragmatically rather than getting stuck in bureaucracy.

We’re looking for someone with strong commercial instincts, a sharp GTM mindset, and the ability to operate comfortably in technical conversations.

This role will own

  • Winning new business

  • Developing and managing our growing sales pipeline

  • Go-to-market strategy and execution

  • Client onboarding and ongoing commercial relationship management

What you will be doing

  • Defining sales at Axle, as we establish our go-to-market approach. You will have the ability to make an immediate contribution to our rapidly increasing revenue growth

  • Owning new customer acquisition end-to-end, from first conversation through to commercial close, setting our partners up to generate meaningful revenue (bonus points if you can do this in multiple languages)

  • Driving go-to-market execution with partners, including value propositions, pricing considerations, customer segmentation, and launch strategies

  • Acting as a commercial bridge between partners and internal teams, translating market and customer insights into clear product, pricing, and GTM inputs

  • Building and refine scalable sales and partner processes that support repeatable growth across different customer segments

  • Tracking performance, pipeline, and outcomes, using data to prioritise effort and continuously improve commercial effectiveness

What success looks like

  • In your first 90 days: you’ll know our product and markets, have built your own pipeline of EV charging, battery and heat-pump partners, and closed your first deal

  • By 6 months: several new partners signed and launched, generating revenue on our platform

  • By 12 months: you own a customer segment end to end, and you’re ready to take on a new market or proposition

Benefits

A meaningful slice of equity in Axle, alongside a competitive salary, with total compensation ranging from £75k–£200k (base salary + equity).

We operate with a deliberately flat structure and aim to keep pay equitable across the company, with a 1:1 median ratio between founder and team compensation.

Enhanced parental leave to support you through life's meaningful moments.

Bi-annual retreats to strengthen team connection & shared purpose.

Hybrid working - We have a dog-friendly office around Farringdon. To maximize collaboration, we ask that you spend 2-3 days a week in the office.

The opportunity to directly shape the future of energy markets and accelerate the transition to a low-carbon world.

We are extremely keen to build a diverse company, and we’re particularly eager to hear from candidates who don't fit the traditional role stereotypes. If you’re motivated by our mission, please do reach out, even if you feel you might not ‘check all the boxes’.

Celerion is committed to swift, exceptional clinical research through translational medicine.  Every day, we use our experience, agility, and innovative research strategies to help get drugs to market faster.  Celerion offers one of the most experienced clinical pharmacology research networks in the industry.
 
Are you looking for an opportunity to support a business creating life-saving treatments? If so, we can't wait to meet you!
Celerion is seeking a full-time experienced SAS Data Analyst to join our Data Management and Biometrics team in Belfast, Northern Ireland and provide SAS statistical support to the project team for analysis and reporting of clinical data in early stage clinical research studies.
 
The primary responsibilities of this position are:
- independently develop, maintain, and process SAS programs for moderately complex studies that create standard and/or customized: edits to clinical checks, analytical data sets, statistical analyses, tables, figures, and electronic data transfers
-assist Senior SAS Data Analysts and Biostatisticians with highly complex projects and perform peer Quality Control functions for output using data from studies with similar characteristics
-also responsible for ensuring strict compliance with study protocol and department procedures
 
An attractive salary and benefits package is available.
 

Education and skills requirements

Cinder is the mission-critical infrastructure that keeps the world's most important digital platforms true to what they stand for. Why this role

Once a deal closes, you're the technical owner on the ground. You're the escalation point for the customer, working closely with their CSM and Agent Product Manager (agent PM), and the first line of engineering defense when something isn't working the way they expect.

For some customers, "close" means embedded. You're effectively part of their engineering team, in their Slack, on their calls, building alongside them. The platforms you'd be embedded with have hundreds of millions of users between them. When you fix something, it's not hypothetical. It's live, that day.

What you'd actually work on

  • Shape and prove the solution. Work directly with customers to understand their problems, identify the right use cases, and build proofs of concept that demonstrate value and de-risk the path to production.

  • Turn fieldwork into product leverage. Solve issues in the systems you ship, identify patterns across customers, and turn those lessons into reusable tools and improvements to the core product. Own on-call for customers when system downtime means moderation stops.

  • 4-8 years as a software engineer, solutions engineer, or in a similar role in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

Location & Benefits

Our team is based in London and we believe that in-person collaboration is important. We offer medical and dental insurance benefits through Allianz Global. We hold at least two all-company events per year. We offer paid lunch when our team is in-person.

What is Flagstone?

Flagstone is many things. An online savings platform, reinventing how individuals, businesses, and charities manage, protect, and grow their cash. A diverse group of people, bound by a collaborative spirit, and shared purpose. And lastly, a thriving, profitable business – where smart people do their best work.

Each definition shares a common thread: our unique culture. It’s our pride and joy. And our competitive advantage.

A feel for our culture

To revolutionise the savings market, we need to be at our best. But high performance takes more than talent – it takes a culture of kindness, respect, and growth.

That’s why we’re building a diverse, inclusive community, where your voice is heard and valued. Where, with close support and room to develop, you can surpass even your own expectations. And be rewarded for it.

We may not change the world, but we can change the world of financial technology. And all it takes is a winning mix of drive, talent, and empathy. Our culture celebrates all three.

But enough about us. Let’s talk about you.

Does this sound like you?

Flagstone is the UK's leading cash platform with £19bn in AuA and a mandate to reach £50bn by 2028. The IFA and wealth manager channel is one of the most significant growth opportunities in front of the business, with over 1,400 registered IFA firms already on the platform and many more still to bring on board.

The role combines proactive business development with ongoing relationship management. On one side, you'll be deepening engagement with our existing base of registered firms, and turning platform access into active, consistent referral behaviour. On the other, you'll be identifying new IFA firms across London and the South East who aren't on Flagstone yet, introducing the proposition and building the relationship from first meeting through to active referral partner.

What You'll Be Doing

Proactive Partner Engagement & Development

  • Own your territory of IFA firms and wealth managers, taking personal responsibility for the breadth and depth of engagement and the referral activity it generates

  • Spend the majority of your time in the field visiting adviser firms, attending regional industry events, and building face-to-face relationships that create consistent, long-term referral partners

  • Deepen engagement with our existing base of registered firms who aren't yet referring regularly, understanding what's holding them back and taking targeted action to unlock their activity

  • Grow the volume and value of referrals from existing active partners by helping them identify more clients who could benefit from Flagstone

  • Identify IFA firms not yet on Flagstone, introducing the proposition and building the relationship from first meeting through to active referral partner

Proposition Training & Education

  • Deliver clear, confident, and compelling presentations of the Flagstone proposition to IFA firms individually and in group settings

  • Train advisers on the Flagstone referral portal and onboarding process, reducing friction and building confidence so that making a referral feels straightforward

  • Keep partner firms up to date with product developments and platform enhancements

  • Use insight from adviser conversations to feed back proposition gaps, platform friction points, or competitive pressures

Reactive Support & Partner Feedback

  • Act as a knowledgeable and responsive point of contact for your partner firms when they have questions about Flagstone, the referral process, or platform features

  • Resolve queries with pace and accuracy, always closing the loop with the adviser

  • Act as a structured source of intelligence from the IFA market back into Flagstone, capturing and communicating what advisers are telling you about the platform, proposition, and competitive landscape

  • Feed adviser feedback directly into the product development process, flagging friction points, missing features, and enhancements that would most meaningfully increase referral activity

Pipeline & Performance

  • Maintain a clear and current picture of your regional pipeline through tracking firm engagement levels, referral volumes, and conversion activity

  • Report regularly to the Relationships Team Lead on the health of your territory - what is working, where the opportunities are, and where support is needed

What You'll Bring

Field Sales & Relationship Management

  • Experience in a field based sales or relationship management role, with a proven track record of building trusted commercial relationships face to face

  • Genuine comfort being out in the field every day, covering a broad and geographically diverse territory - you need to be energised by travel, variety, and independence

  • The personal presence and communication skills to represent Flagstone confidently in front of independent financial advisers and wealth managers

Financial Services Knowledge

  • You don't need direct cash management experience to succeed in this role, that can be trained. What matters more is a genuine track record of building trusted adviser relationships, whether that's from a platform, wrap, DFM, or a wider intermediary facing background.

  • Familiarity with the regulatory landscape: directly authorised firms, Appointed Representatives, and network members

  • Financial literacy to have credible, confident conversations with advisers about how the Flagstone proposition fits within their clients' wider financial planning

Commercial Drive & Self-Direction

  • A commercially motivated self-starter who takes personal ownership of regional performance and manages their own diary and territory plan

  • Organised and disciplined in how you manage a complex regional portfolio: you plan your visits, track your pipeline, and follow up consistently across a large number of relationships simultaneously

How we reward you:

At Flagstone, the benefits extend beyond false gifts like “fruit and snacks”. Instead, we invest in your health, wealth, and professional development. Here’s a selection of our benefits:

  • Competitive bonus scheme - designed to reward and recognise high performance

  • Flexible benefits budget - a pot to fund meaningful benefits for you, whether it's hormone or fertility testing, cancer screening, neuro-diversity coaching or something that matters for you.

  • A range of salary sacrifice options to help you make tax efficient savings on electric cars, nursery schemes, home and tech goods.

  • Around the World scheme - 3 months work from anywhere scheme

  • Mental wellbeing support - Access therapy and mental health sessions through Spill

  • Learning and development - £1,000 personal development budget to help you grow in your role.

  • Private health care - Enjoy all the benefits AXA has to offer, including reduced gym memberships and medical history disregarded

  • Medical cash plan - To help you with the costs of dental and optical expenses

  • Life insurance and Income Protection- four times your annual salary for peace of mind

  • Matched pension contributions up to 5%

  • 25 days holiday - plus bank holidays, well-being days and volunteering days

  • Enhanced Parental Leave - enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption pay.  

All are welcome.

At Flagstone, we’re assembling a diverse team that defies our industry’s norms. Think this role could suit you? We encourage you to apply, no matter your background.

The Senior Theatre Practitioner – Anaesthetics is responsible for delivering safe, high-quality anaesthetic support across theatre services, with flexibility to provide assistance in Recovery as required.

This role provides senior clinical leadership, supervising and mentoring junior staff, non-registered support staff, and students, while contributing to service improvement, maintaining operational efficiency, and ensuring compliance with mandatory training, policies, and SOPs.

The post holder is professionally accountable in accordance with the NMC / HCPC Code of Professional Conduct and ensures alignment with national guidance.

The post holder will work within a highly specialised Orthopaedic and Spinal surgical environment, delivering safe and effective perioperative care to patients undergoing complex procedures. The role requires the ability to perform efficiently in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment, responding effectively to changing clinical priorities, emergency situations, and demanding surgical workloads while maintaining professionalism, attention to detail, and patient safety at all times. 

Clinical Responsibilities

  • Provide expert anaesthetic support, including preparation, monitoring, and assisting during procedures.

  • Support scrub and circulating staff throughout the perioperative period.

  • Actively participate in emergency response teams. Including allocated resuscitation roles and daily safety huddles.

  • Deliver patient assessment, planning, implementation, and evaluation throughout the anaesthetic care pathway.

  • Provide assistance in Recovery/Enhanced Care as required to support patient safety and flow.

  • Maintain up-to-date skills and knowledge in anaesthetics and recovery care.

  • Participate in the on-call rota and support flexible working arrangements.

  • Maintain accurate, contemporaneous patient documentation in line with policy.

  • Ensure safe handling, storage, and administration of medications.

  • Conduct pre-use checks of all anaesthetic equipment and escalate faults promptly.

  • Participate in audit, quality improvement initiatives, and action plan implementation.

  • Maintain 100% compliance with mandatory training, national guidance, and organisational policy.

Leadership & People Management

  • Deputise for the Lead or Deputy Lead Practitioner when required.

  • Provide clinical supervision and mentorship to junior colleagues, non-registered support staff, and students.

  • Contribute to staff appraisal, development planning, and competency assessments.

  • Support orientation of new staff, bank, and agency colleagues.

  • Promote a professional, inclusive, and collaborative team culture.

MDT Collaboration & Team Support

  • Work closely with surgeons, theatre staff, anaesthetists, recovery nurses, and wider MDT to ensure safe, coordinated patient care.

  • Support colleagues during periods of high activity or staffing pressures.

  • Communicate effectively across departments to ensure smooth theatre operations.

Governance, Risk & Compliance

  • Adhere to all private-sector policies, SOPs, and national guidance including NICE, NatSSIPs, LocSSIPs, NCEPOD, RCoA.

  • Report incidents, near misses, and risks promptly, contributing to investigations and learning outcomes.

  • Ensure practice is evidence-based, up to date with clinical standards, and aligned with organisational procedures.

  • Participate in policy updates and service development initiatives to improve patient care and operational efficiency.

  • Maintain confidentiality and GDPR compliance at all times.

Operational & Financial Responsibilities

  • Contribute to effective theatre management, including coordination of patient lists, equipment, and consumables.

  • Support revenue capture and ensure accurate use of resources.

  • Identify requirements for new or replacement equipment, escalating where appropriate.

  • Assist with service improvement projects within agreed timeframes and budgets.


Knowledge, Skills & Experience

  • Registered Practitioner with NMC or HCPC registration.

  • Minimum 4 years post-qualification experience in an operating theatre environment.

  • Proven experience in supporting complex elective surgical pathways in a high-throughput theatre environment

  • Degree-level qualification or equivalent professional experience

  • Strong clinical reasoning and decision-making skills across a varied patient caseload

  • Experience supervising and mentoring junior staff and students

  • Demonstrable ability to work autonomously and take clinical leadership responsibility for anaesthetic services on shift

  • Evidence of Continuous Professional Development (CPD)

  • Immediate Life Support qualification

  • Advanced Life Support qualification (or commitment to work towards)

  • Commitment to 100% compliance with mandatory training, policies, and SOPs.

  • Mentorship / Practice Assessor qualification

  • Sedation course

  • Experience in budgetary management, service improvement, or revenue capture

  • Experience supporting or leading clinical audits, quality improvement, or service redesign projects

     

** We are pleased to offer a £4,000 joining bonus for this position, subject to Fortius’ terms and conditions. Additionally, if you refer someone who is successfully appointed to the role, you may also be eligible for a referral bonus, subject to the applicable referral scheme terms and conditions. **

raw.title: Data Engineer
raw.description:
Data Engineer

London (Waterloo) · Full-time · Hybrid, three days per week in the office

Who we are

At GetGround, our mission is to make property investment safer, faster and more accessible for everyone.

We’ve built an all-in-one property investment platform that supports investors from opportunity analysis and company formation through to financing, accounting and portfolio management. By bringing software, data and specialist services into one experience, we make property investing simpler, clearer and more cost-effective.

We’re now building the intelligence layer that will help investors understand opportunities, make better decisions and manage their portfolios. We bring together detailed knowledge of our customers’ investments, services such as mortgages, lettings and insurance, and a team that lives and breathes property.

We’re turning our property expertise into an intelligence layer that can scale. That starts with a data platform: selecting trusted sources, keeping information current and making it useful to our products and AI agents.

We’re looking for someone to own that foundation.

The opportunity

You’ll define and build the data platform that powers GetGround’s intelligence layer. This is a hands-on role with substantial architectural ownership: choosing how we ingest, structure, curate and serve data, while improving the foundations we already have.

The scope goes beyond integrating with APIs. You’ll build ways to ingest unstructured policy updates, regulatory guidance and published documents, turning them into reliable data our intelligence layer can use.

You’ll work closely with engineering, product and our property experts to turn domain knowledge into useful data. You’ll also design for international expansion, so entering each new market builds on a shared platform.

There’s an opportunity to influence how we build our data organisation over time, including the capabilities, standards and future hires we need.

What you’ll do

  • Own data as a product. Start with the decisions our customers and AI agents need to make, then work backwards to the data required. Judge success by the usefulness and reliability of what you enable.

  • Be opinionated about sources and quality. Work with our property experts to identify the most valuable datasets and assess their authority, coverage, freshness and limitations. Establish clear standards for what enters the platform and how conflicting information is handled.

  • Build ingestion beyond APIs. Develop reliable pipelines for structured datasets, external APIs, documents and published guidance. Ingest updates from sources such as HMRC and other relevant authorities, detecting changes promptly and turning them into usable, traceable data.

  • Make data usable by our intelligence layer. Structure and serve information so our products and AI agents can retrieve the right facts in context. Preserve source provenance, geographic scope and effective dates so consumers can distinguish current information from historical or superseded guidance.

  • Design for international expansion. Build shared models and ingestion patterns that accommodate differences in property markets, tax systems and regulation. When we expand geographies, we want to go at speed, without rebuilding the platform.

  • Own reliability throughout the lifecycle. Build monitoring, validation and recovery into ingestion, transformation, storage and serving. Know what is stale, missing or incorrect, understand the customer impact and address the root cause.

  • Set the technical direction and deliver it. Make clear trade-offs between immediate product needs and long-term architecture. Ship useful improvements early, document decisions and help shape the standards and future team needed to support the platform.

What you bring

  • Experience owning substantial data systems. You’ve designed, built and operated production data platforms or major parts of them, and can explain the architectural decisions you made and their consequences.

  • Strong engineering fundamentals. You bring strong SQL, data modelling and production programming skills, with practical experience in orchestration, testing, deployment and operating reliable pipelines.

  • Judgment about the data itself. You can evaluate whether a source is fit for a particular use, reconcile inconsistent information and make uncertainty or gaps visible to downstream consumers.

  • Experience with messy external sources. You’ve handled inconsistent formats, changing schemas, incomplete records, rate limits and integration failures. You’re comfortable working beyond clean, well-documented APIs.

  • A product mindset. You care about the decisions your data supports. You can work with domain experts and product engineers to translate an ambiguous need into a useful data product.

  • Architectural ownership. You can review an existing system, establish a direction and deliver improvements incrementally. You understand access controls, privacy and the responsibilities that come with combining customer and external data.

  • Clear communication and initiative. You surface problems early, write down decisions and challenge assumptions constructively. You’re comfortable making progress without a fully specified ticket.

Bonus

  • Experience building data foundations for AI products, including retrieval, document processing or evaluating the quality of information supplied to agents.

  • Experience modelling policy or regulatory information, including versioning and effective dates.

  • Experience with property, financial services, geospatial data or international datasets.

  • Familiarity with GCP, where we run our infrastructure, and experience working alongside backend engineering teams.

  • Experience establishing data standards or helping build a data team.

This role isn’t for you if

  • You just want to keep the pipelines running. You’ll need to care about which data we use, whether it can be trusted and how it improves the decisions our products support.

  • You want a fully specified architecture to implement. We need someone who can assess what exists, challenge assumptions and take ownership of the technical direction.

  • You only want to work with clean, structured data. Important information arrives through documents, policy announcements and inconsistent external sources. Making it usable is part of the job.

  • You want to stay removed from the product or domain. You’ll work closely with product engineers and property experts. Understanding what the data means and how it is used is essential.

  • You don’t connect with how we work. Our values—No BS, pursuit of excellence, feedback obsessed and healthy ego—mean communicating directly, holding a high bar, seeking feedback and being willing to change your mind.

Why join

  • Own a data platform central to GetGround’s next phase of product development.

  • Turn deep property expertise into intelligence that helps real investors.

  • Work on challenging problems across customer data, property information, AI and regulated services.

  • Shape the architecture for international expansion and help build our future data organisation.

  • Competitive salary and meaningful equity.

  • Hybrid London working, with three days per week in Waterloo.

  • Benefits include private health and dental cover, a learning budget, a home-office setup budget and 12 mental health days per year.

What we are building: The first end-to-end real estate investment offering - making the dream of owning real estate more accessible to everyone globally.

Diversity & inclusion at GetGround: We encourage applications from all sections of society and we believe in the criticality of an inclusive culture. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity or any other basis as protected by law.

This is a high impact, visible role. As our Strategy & Operations Manager, you'll support the CEO & COO and augment their capacity by taking on problems to solve that are critically important to how we build all aspects of GetGround. Some weeks that means building the model that decides whether we enter a new market. Others it means untangling why a core funnel is leaking, or writing the board paper, or problem solving what seems like the impossible task. raw.title: Treasury Lead
raw.description:
About Griffin

Hi, we’re Griffin. We’re a fully regulated UK bank that powers the accounts and payments offerings of product-led fintechs and platforms like Uber, Yonder, Prosper, and Sidekick. By doing the heavy lifting behind the scenes, our customers can focus on what they do best - delivering amazing customer experiences.

We’ve grown rapidly since our launch in 2024, and today provide the banking backbone behind products in remittance, payroll, wealth, insurance, proptech, payments, neobanking and more.

We’re moving into card issuing, stablecoin infrastructure, and agentic finance next as we continue to support the next generation of product-led companies.

Learn more about what we do

Our culture

We believe that smart, motivated, conscientious people thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments and have done our best to create such an environment at Griffin. People who thrive here don’t require much hand-holding, and go out of their way to figure out how to contribute in the most valuable way possible.

We've been remote-first since we were established in 2017 and we remain so today. Work here is asynchronous and fully flexible - because we want to be a part of your life in a way that helps you to get the most out of both your work and home life.

We understand that our culture and ways of working aren’t for everyone, and we’re very intentional about our hiring process as a result. We won't hire people who don’t seem like a strong fit for our core values, even if they're otherwise extremely qualified.

Our strong culture has helped us to remain a mission-driven company as we have scaled, and gives our people a clear, explicit operating framework and the space to focus on delivering real value for our customers.

Learn more about our culture.

The Team

Our vision is that our Finance team plays a central part of the business, somewhere the Board can rely on to support strategic planning. In this our treasury team keeps us safely funded and liquid and gives the Board and ALCO numbers they can trust. As we add products and markets, the team is growing. As second hire to the team, you’ll report directly to our Treasurer, sitting at the heart of how we capture, report, analyse and manage risk to support how we optimise Griffin’s balance sheet.

The opportunity

Treasury at a fintech bank is different. You’ll see real-time payment flows and deposit behaviour that a conventional bank never sees. You’ll work directly with our Treasurer to build our treasury processes, reporting and systems rather than inherit them. You’ll contribute to management of liquidity as a Direct FPS participant, use of facilities within the Bank of England’s Sterling Monetary Framework (SMF), card issuing and stablecoin infrastructure.

What success looks like

By month 3, you’ll understand our business and processes, run daily reporting with Michael’s review and handle daily cash positioning, including our Bank of England reserve account. By month 6, you’ll own daily and monthly reporting and run intraday cash management independently, including testing the SMF. You’ll have drafted ALCO papers and credit reviews, delivered your first automation improvements and contributed to the impact assessment for Direct FPS or a similar product launch.

To do this you’ll own

  • Daily and intraday reporting on liquidity, capital, interest rate risk, funding capacity and asset encumbrance, with every output sense-checked before it goes out

  • Risk monitoring against our risk appetite: limits, triggers and early warning indicators, forecast-versus-actual reviews, and stress tests you design with the Treasurer

  • Intraday cash management and liquidity forecasting: cash positioning, payments and transfers, depositor behaviour and outflow assumptions

  • Monthly management reporting, including interest income, margin and customer profitability, the ALCO pack, inputs to regulatory returns, and contributions to the ILAAP and ICAAP

  • Dealing operations: pre- and post-trade checks, confirmations, settlements and collateral movements, plus credit analysis on counterparties and issuers. You’ll also cover for the Treasurer with brokers, treasury bill auctions and SMF drawdowns

  • Automating manual steps, closing control gaps, and documenting procedures that mean knowledge never sits with just two people

  • Maintaining our treasury bank and broker mandates

We expect you to shape this role

This description reflects what we need today. How you achieve these outcomes, where you focus your energy, how this role evolves—that's for you to define as you learn what our customers need and where our technical gaps are.

Your background

To succeed in the role, we're looking for people who have:

  • 5+ years in a bank treasury function (e.g. middle-office, ALM or balance sheet management), measuring and reporting liquidity and capital from economic and regulatory perspectives. You will have produced reports hands-on rather than reviewed them

  • Strong prudential knowledge across liquidity, capital and leverage (e.g. CRR, Basel III, LCR, NSFR, IRRBB, ILAAP, ICAAP), and hands-on exposure to the dealing lifecycle: pre- and post-trade checks, confirmations and settlements

  • Advanced Excel skills (e.g. data tables, scenario analysis, VBA), plus the attention to detail and reconciliation discipline to sense-check everything you produce

  • An analytical, inquisitive mindset, with a habit of automating what’s manual

  • The organisation and drive to work autonomously, remotely and asynchronously, and the appetite for the breadth and ambiguity of building in an early-stage bank

  • A love of writing - we have a major amount of written documentation that you will be contributing to, and we place a high degree of importance on clarity and readability (you can find out more here about how we write )

Ideally, you would also:

  • Hold a treasury or accountancy qualification (ACT, CertBALM, FRM, CFA, ACA, ACCA or CIMA)

  • Bring Python, SQL, Power BI or AI skills

  • Knowledge of Direct FPS and Bank of England SMF facilities

  • Experience implementing or using treasury or ALM systems

What can we offer you?

  • Remote-first flexibility: Work from anywhere in the UK

  • Work from abroad: Up to 20 days a year

  • Time off: 28 days’ holiday + bank holidays

  • Share options: Own a part of what we’re building together

  • Pension: Auto-enrolment into our Penfold scheme

  • Insurance: Private medical with Bupa (including family cover) and life insurance with AIG

  • Wellbeing: 1:1 coaching and therapy session available through Oliva

  • Family leave: Enhanced parental leave with up to 6 months on full pay after two years’ service

  • AI tools: Everyone has a Claude subscription on us and access to other premium tools

  • Your setup: We’ll support you in creating a comfortable and effective WFH environment.

As a bank, we’re committed to maintaining the highest standards of security. This means that the successful candidate will need to complete background screening, and our offer will be conditional upon satisfactory review of these checks. This would include verification of right to work, criminal record, credit history, social media and professional reference checks.

How long will the process take?

We move as fast as possible, but it normally takes us about 2-3 weeks to get to know to each other.

  • Step 1: An initial phone call with our Talent Team for us to tell you more about Griffin and learn about your recent experience.

  • Step 2: Meet your manager to talk through your experience and how that relates to the requirements.

  • Step 3: A task based on what you’ll be doing on a day to day at Griffin.

  • Step 4: Meet with peers in your team for a more in-depth technical interview.

  • Step 5: Culture and Founder interview: Learn more about this here.

How do I apply?

Are we your next move? Apply via the link below, if there's a match our Talent team will reach out to schedule an initial conversation and talk you through what happens next.

We don’t work with recruitment agencies, so please don’t send us speculative CVs.

Under representation

At Griffin, we’re looking for people who instinctively vibe with our values, behaviours and mission. You’re encouraged to apply, even if your experience doesn’t tick every box. Careers, like life, can take many twists and turns. Your technical expertise and path to where you are today will stand out. We're committed to creating a place where everyone belongs and we welcome diverse perspectives, backgrounds and people who are ready to build a global platform for programmable finance

raw.title: Cyber Essentials Plus Lead Assessor (IASME licensed)
raw.description:
Intelance is a UK advisory and assurance firm and an IASME licensed Certification Body for Cyber Essentials and Cyber Essentials Plus. We are adding experienced Cyber Essentials Plus Lead Assessors to our associate panel to lead UK client assessments from start to finish.

This is an associate contractor role. Work is offered assessment by assessment, with no guaranteed volume. Each assignment is covered by a written statement of work that sets out the scope, timetable, location and fee before you accept it.

Tasks

  • Lead Cyber Essentials Plus assessments from scoping to certificate decision, in line with the current IASME and NCSC test specification.

  • Check the Cyber Essentials self assessment and confirm the Cyber Essentials Plus scope is correct before testing starts.

  • Work out the device sample and plan testing of user devices, internet gateways, cloud services and public facing services.

  • Carry out remote and onsite testing, authenticated vulnerability scans and evidence checks.

  • Record findings clearly, agree fixes with the client and manage retesting within the permitted timescale.

  • Write complete assessment records and clear client reports.

  • Review the work of other assessors on the panel before results are submitted, and give them practical feedback.

  • Handle the larger and more complex assessments, such as multi site organisations and mixed Windows, macOS, Linux and mobile estates.

  • Work through Intelance accounts, systems and quality checks, and protect all client information.

  • Tell us about any conflict of interest before you accept an assignment.

Requirements

Essential

  • Current IASME appointment as a Cyber Essentials Assessor and a Cyber Essentials Plus Assessor. We will check this with IASME.

  • At least two years of delivering Cyber Essentials Plus assessments, with 20 or more completed in the last 12 months.

  • Experience reviewing or signing off other assessors' work, or acting as Lead Assessor for a Certification Body.

  • Based in the UK and able to attend client sites in the UK when an assessment needs it.

  • Strong hands on knowledge of Windows, macOS, Microsoft 365, Entra ID, Intune, firewalls, cloud services, multi factor authentication and vulnerability scanning.

  • Able to explain findings in plain English to business owners and IT teams.

  • Professional Indemnity and Public Liability insurance of at least £1m each before any client work starts.

  • Two recent references for Cyber Essentials Plus work.

Useful

  • CISSP, CISM, CREST, OSCP, ISO 27001 Lead Auditor or another qualification accepted on the IASME assessor route.

  • Experience with Qualys, Tenable Nessus or a similar approved scanning tool.

  • IASME Cyber Assurance assessor status.

Benefits

  • Day rate of £375 to £550, or a fixed fee for each assessment agreed before you accept the work.

  • A steady flow of scoped assessments from an established Certification Body, with no sales work for you to do.

  • Remote preparation and reporting, with site visits only when the assessment needs them.

  • Access to Intelance templates, scanning capability, secure collaboration tools and quality review.

  • A clear route to a trusted associate role and more senior assurance work across ISO 27001 and IASME Cyber Assurance.

  • You choose which assignments you accept.

Apply with your CV and answer the short screening questions. Shortlisted applicants will be asked for IASME assessor evidence and two references. Please do not send any client material.

By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide.

It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone.

🐙 Kraken Generation Flex

The energy industry is undergoing the largest transformation since industrialisation, at an unprecedented rate of change and we are positioning ourselves at the heart of it. In the UK, with a legally binding Net Zero target for 2050 and a clean-power ambition for 2030, we are scaling rapidly to integrate Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) into the grid.

Kraken is recognised as a thought leader and innovator. With complete independence from Octopus Energy, we are building a SaaS business that digitally connects hundreds of thousands of DERs with energy markets. As our UK fleet grows and we support our expansion across Europe, we are looking for an Integrations Engineer to help turn customer sites into market-connected, controllable assets.

🏠 Where you’ll fit in and role summary

As we scale our fleet of integrated assets, we are looking for an Electrical Engineer to support the delivery of our site integrations and grow into owning them, learning the full lifecycle from the early information stage through design, deployment and testing.

You’ll be part of an engineering delivery team, based in Manchester, who take an integration project from the very early information stage, design how it will be integrated into Kraken’s platform and then turn that design into a live, controllable, market-participating asset.

Engineering delivery is an innovative and engineering-focused team with a culture that fosters collaboration and fresh thinking to create a new energy system. Alongside design, deployment and testing; they constantly look into ways to improve efficiency through tooling and the automation of repetitive tasks. They collaborate daily with delivery managers and customer success to onboard new sites as well as support the existing.

🚀 What you'll own

  • Integration design contribution: With guidance, analyse provided information and contribute to hardware and software integration approaches. When necessary, exchange information with customer technical representatives through meetings and emails, and take part in design discussions with other team members.

  • Technical judgement: Develop your technical judgement, making well-reasoned decisions and trade-offs with support from senior engineers, and contributing technical input to discussions within the team.

  • Developing domain knowledge: Build up your knowledge in one or more technical areas. This could include grid regulations (G99, G100, Grid Code etc.), energy markets, multi BMUs, industrial communication protocols, industrial networking, internet of things, cyber security and so on.

  • Gateway application & configuration: Learn how the Gateway software (developed by an internal software team) works and how it is configured. Understand the requirements for an integration and judge if the gateway software is able to support it or will need new development work. The team will help you get gateway configuration literate and you will carry out deployments and changes independently over time.

  • Hardware and Software Deployments: Learn the process of our hardware and software deployments. Over time, take ownership of the configuration, deployment and testing with guidance from the senior engineers.

  • Networking and cyber security: Contribute to hardware and network connectivity designs, keeping our own cyber security posture in mind as well as addressing the concerns from customers, with the support of the internal security team.

  • Site testing & commissioning: Carry out site testing and commissioning initially with the support of the team and building toward doing this independently as onboarding demand grows.

  • Incidents & compliance: Help address engineering help requests from other teams and support incident response in the case of issues at existing sites.

🧠 What you'll bring to the party

  • Understanding of the Regulations: Working knowledge of the UK Grid Code, G99 and the other obligations of a grid-connected asset before it can participate in the energy markets.

  • Understanding of the UK Energy Markets: Working understanding of the NESO ancillary services (Dynamic Containment / Moderation / Regulation, Firm Frequency Response), the Balancing Mechanism, and the DNO connection/integration process.

  • Technical judgement: Sound technical judgement and a structured approach to problems, working with the team to agree and implement a solution.

  • Power plant systems: Ability to read and analyse single line diagrams for a given power plant to understand the site architecture for the points of metering and control instrumentation.

  • Asset integration: Exposure to, or a keen interest in, integrating BESS (grid-scale and/or C&I) and/or RES (Wind and Solar) for telemetry and control.

  • Integration design: Ability to contribute to clear integration designs and design documentation.

  • Hardware and Networking: Familiarity with control systems deployments and their connectivity including the local networking and cyber security aspects, and an ability to help debug site connectivity and networking issues (including 4G routers and firewalls) with support.

  • Industrial Communication Protocols: Practical experience or a good working knowledge of Modbus (TCP/RTU); awareness of one or more of IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 61400-25, OPC-UA or DNP3 is a plus.

  • CAD, Diagrams and Tools: Experience or familiarity with CAD tools such as AutoCAD or BricsCAD, Miro and Notion.

  • Communication: A clear communicator who documents their work (e.g. in design docs and Notion) and collaborates well with the team.

  • Commissioning landscape: Awareness of the other parties involved in site commissioning for power plants, their roles and responsibilities, and how we work with them.

  • Engineering background: Bachelor's in Electrical Engineering, Automation/Control, Software, or a related field - or equivalent practical experience in industrial/energy integration.

  • A proactive and collaborative mindset: You are eager to learn and grow, reliable and collaborative. You take initiative, communicate openly, raise risks early, and care about safe working. You welcome feedback, support your teammates, and steadily build toward taking on more independent ownership of integrations over time.

  • Travel: Willingness to travel to customers and sites although travel is very occasional. Awareness of site safety is required as we may work with site personnel even though we are remote.

⭐️ Bonus points

  • Wider knowledge of grid compliance (G99, G100, Grid Code) and where the Kraken system fits in.

  • Experience with AWS IoT Greengrass or similar edge-deployment architectures.

  • Familiarity with software/scripting and templating (e.g. Python, Rust, the Linux command line) and Git-based workflows.

  • Understanding of IT/OT security in the energy sector (IEC 62443, NIS Regulations awareness).

  • Exposure to wider European balancing markets / ENTSO-E frameworks and TSO integrations.

raw.title: Staff Frontend Engineer
raw.description:
About Motorway

Motorway is the UK's largest online car-selling platform. We connect private sellers directly with over 8,000 dealers nationwide. Our online platform helps sellers achieve great prices for their cars while giving dealers fast, reliable access to the stock they want for their dealerships. Founded in 2017, our award-winning, technology-led approach has redefined the experience of selling a car. Motorway is backed by some of the world’s leading technology investors, having raised £143 million in Series C funding.

This is a unique opportunity to join a fast-growing scale-up at a crucial phase of growth and help change an industry for the better.

We're looking for a Staff Frontend Engineer to help lead technically across our frontend engineering. You'll work across a group of cross-functional squads, each made up of engineers, designers, data analysts and a product manager, helping them move quickly and safely, resolving the engineering problems that span teams before they compound into systemic risk, and shaping product and business strategy with a technically-grounded, commercially-aware point of view.

We're a TypeScript-first organisation. Our frontend stack is TypeScript and React, styled with SCSS, server-side rendered with Next.js and Express, and tested with Vitest & Chromatic. As a Staff engineer you'll bring deep expertise with the latest native web technologies and modern frameworks, drive consistency across all of our web properties, and lead the migration efforts that keep our stack current, not just bumping versions, but making use of the new capabilities each release brings and helping the wider department do the same.

At Motorway, we know the importance of delivering high-quality, valuable solutions quickly, and we recognise the ability for AI tools and agents to accelerate our work. We provide our engineers with access to the latest models through Kiro. As a Staff engineer you'll define and lead our AI engineering practice on the frontend, setting standards for agent execution environments, quality harnesses, and guardrail architecture - and build a team norm where domain depth, AI-enabled breadth, and rigorous feedback-loop design are treated as complementary.

What you'll be doing

  • Ship features end to end: Own meaningful pieces of product work from design handoff through to production, building accessible, performant components, wiring them into applications, and shipping them with confidence.

  • Author the contracts and the roadmap: Author and own API contracts and documentation for the department, and maintain a technical roadmap with rigorous written framing - precise intent, explicit trade-offs, and unambiguous success criteria - setting the documentation and spec-writing standard for the area.

  • Drive consistency and lead migrations: Drive consistency across all our web properties, design the standards the department builds on, and lead migration efforts - making full use of new framework features and bringing the rest of engineering along with you.

  • Own quality, security, performance and reliability standards: Set and maintain the security & web performance standards for the frontend, including client-side concerns like CSP, CWV, XSS prevention, data, governance plus reliability standards, incident review culture, and production readiness criteria.

  • Own the build and deployment story: Understand the build and deployment pipeline for our assets and services end to end, monitor and improve it, and make informed, commercially-aware decisions about hosting providers, vendors, and build-vs-buy trade-offs.

  • Develop other engineers: Develop IC3 engineers into technical leaders, raise the technical bar in hiring by defining what "good" looks like in the discipline, and build a culture of ownership, accountability, and high standards.

  • Lead AI-assisted engineering: Use Kiro and other AI tools to move faster, and set the standards for how the team integrates AI into its everyday workflow and its products.

What you'll have

Minimum requirements

  • At least 5+ years of experience in focused frontend practice building and operating production web applications at scale, with a track record of leading large, complex projects.

  • The ability to bridge engineering and product fluently, translating between business priorities and technical constraints in both directions, and to make and defend difficult technical decisions under uncertainty through reasoning, not authority.

  • Recognised as a technical authority in frontend engineering - engineers and product stakeholders seek you out for technical direction, and your judgement shapes decisions beyond your immediate team.

  • Deep expertise with modern CSS/SCSS, HTML, and current ECMAScript proposals, and a strong understanding of the trade-offs between different frameworks and the scenarios in which each is the right choice.

  • Comprehensive experience writing unit and E2E tests, and building the CI workflows to exercise them.

  • Deep working knowledge of TypeScript and modern React (hooks, component composition, transitions), and of frameworks like Next.js that handle SSR, routing, and data fetching.

  • Deep experience with observability, Core Web Vitals, accessibility auditing, and frontend performance tuning - and the ability to evaluate new frameworks and identify where we gain an edge in development, deployment, rendering, integration, and performance.

  • Breadth across different teams, and the judgement to make pragmatic build-vs-refactor-vs-replace calls informed by a track record of production crises and scale challenges.

  • A genuine interest in leading AI-assisted development as part of your and the team's workflow.

Additional or preferred requirements

  • Experience owning and maintaining a design system, and driving its adoption across multiple teams.

  • The ability to create sensible UI designs without a Designer for non-trivial (though not highly complex) work when the team is resource-constrained.

  • Experience evaluating vendors and third-party tools, and making build-vs-buy recommendations with clear technical and commercial criteria.

  • Experience maintaining and evolving complex legacy systems at scale.

  • Backend fluency - you don't need to be full-stack, but you're comfortable following a request deep into the API layer and shaping the contract on both sides.
